summary.solution: The patch changes _default_manager to _base_manager in ForeignKey.validate(), exactly matching the root cause identified. It also adds a validation model with a filtering default manager plus regression tests for ForeignKey and OneToOneField (which inherits validate from ForeignKey).
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location and adds meaningful regression tests; all validation and related test suites pass.

defects.description: The added test methods contain trailing whitespace on several blank lines (flagged by git apply). Purely cosmetic, no behavioral impact.
defects.suggestion: Strip trailing whitespace from the new test lines in tests/validation/tests.py.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/related.py, ForeignObject.deconstruct() called self.remote_field.model.lower() which lowercased the entire 'app_label.ModelName' string, corrupting mixed-case app labels (e.g. 'DJ_RegLogin.Category' -> 'dj_reglogin.category'), causing a lazy-reference ValueError during migrate.
summary.solution: The patch replaces the blanket .lower() with make_model_tuple() for dotted references, which lowercases only the model name and preserves the app_label case, producing 'DJ_RegLogin.category'. Bare (no-dot) references keep the previous .lower() behavior. This is exactly the root-cause location and matches the intended fix.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of creation and passes all relevant tests (1321) plus added regression tests; recommend approval.

summary.problem: In django/db/backends/base/operations.py convert_durationfield_value, duration-only expressions (e.g. F('estimated_time') + timedelta) on SQLite return a str representation of a timedelta (produced by _sqlite_format_dtdelta returning str(out), e.g. '2 days, 0:00:00'), which the converter cannot turn into a timedelta, raising TypeError/decimal.InvalidOperation.
summary.solution: The patch updates convert_durationfield_value to keep the existing int microseconds path (datetime.timedelta(0,0,value)) and adds an else branch that parses the timedelta string form via django.utils.dateparse.parse_duration. This is applied at the DB->Python conversion boundary rather than at the value-creation site (_sqlite_format_dtdelta). It is functionally correct: parse_duration correctly parses Python timedelta str formats and the int path preserves behavior for other backends.
summary.overall_assessment: The fix resolves the reported bug end-to-end on SQLite with all relevant tests passing (expressions: 141, db_functions: 299) and no regressions; the conversion hook is a legitimate normalization boundary, so the fix is acceptable despite an alternative cleaner root-cause location existing.

defects.description: The fix handles a SQLite-specific quirk (a timedelta string returned by _sqlite_format_dtdelta) inside the generic base converter. A cleaner root-cause fix would make _sqlite_format_dtdelta return microseconds for duration-only results so all backends yield a uniform int, keeping the base converter simple.
defects.suggestion: Optionally, in django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py _sqlite_format_dtdelta, when the result is a datetime.timedelta return duration_microseconds(out) instead of str(out); then the base converter can remain int-only.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/expressions.py, BaseExpression._resolve_output_field infers the intermediate temporal subtraction (DateTimeField SUB DateTimeField) as DateTimeField instead of DurationField, so combining it with a DurationField Value raises FieldError: mixed types.
summary.solution: The patch adds a _resolve_output_field override on CombinedExpression that returns DurationField when the connector is SUB and both operands are the same temporal field (DateField/DateTimeField/TimeField), otherwise delegates to super(). This makes the intermediate subtraction resolve to DurationField so the outer '+ DurationField' no longer sees mixed types. This is exactly the root-cause location and matches the reviewer's proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the point where the wrong output field is created; all related test suites pass and the reported case now works and returns the correct value.

summary.problem: In django/http/response.py, HttpResponseBase.delete_cookie() does not propagate the cookie's samesite attribute (and does not force Secure for SameSite=None), so deletion cookies drop SameSite and get rejected/ignored by browsers.
summary.solution: The patch adds a samesite=None parameter to delete_cookie() and threads it through to set_cookie(), and updates the messages storage and sessions middleware callers to pass settings.SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE. This matches the root-cause location and fixes the default (SameSite=Lax) messages case. However, it does NOT set secure=True when samesite == 'none', so delete_cookie(samesite='None') still emits a SameSite=None cookie without Secure.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch is at the correct root-cause location but is incomplete: it leaves the exact SameSite=None-without-Secure scenario the issue warns about, so browsers will still ignore such deletion cookies.

defects.description: delete_cookie() computes secure only from the key prefix (__Secure-/__Host-). When called with samesite='None', it produces 'Set-Cookie: ...; SameSite=None' WITHOUT the Secure flag. This is exactly the case the problem statement says Chrome/Firefox will reject/ignore, so cookies deleted with SameSite=None are not reliably removed. Verified: response.delete_cookie('mycookie', samesite='None') yields secure='' (no Secure attribute).
defects.suggestion: In django/http/response.py delete_cookie(), set secure = key.startswith(('__Secure-', '__Host-')) or (samesite and samesite.lower() == 'none'), matching the official fix so SameSite=None deletion cookies are also marked Secure.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py, encode() always produced the new Django 3.1 signing.dumps() format, so setting DEFAULT_HASHING_ALGORITHM='sha1' during transition was not enough: session data written by a 3.1 instance could not be decoded by pre-3.1 instances.
summary.solution: The patch adds a _legacy_encode() method that reproduces the pre-3.1 base64(hash:serialized) format and makes encode() dispatch to it when settings.DEFAULT_HASHING_ALGORITHM == 'sha1'. This is exactly at the root cause (the point of session-data creation) and mirrors the existing _legacy_decode(), matching my proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; all 384 session tests pass and round-trip encode/decode interoperability is verified.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/files.py, FileField.__init__ immediately evaluates a callable `storage` and discards the original callable, so deconstruct() inlines the evaluated Storage instead of returning the callable reference.
summary.solution: The patch stores the original callable as self._storage_callable in __init__ (point of creation) before evaluating it, and deconstruct() emits self._storage_callable when set, otherwise the storage instance (unless it is default_storage). This matches the identified root cause exactly and mirrors the existing upload_to callable behavior.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; deconstruction now returns the callable, reconstruction re-evaluates it, and default/instance storages behave as before. All 626 relevant tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/json.py, KeyTransform had no dedicated `__in` lookup, so the default lookups.In did not wrap rhs values with JSON_EXTRACT/JSON_VALUE/JSON_QUERY on MySQL, Oracle and SQLite (as KeyTransformExact does), causing value__key__in=[0] to return no rows while value__key=0 matched.
summary.solution: The patch adds a KeyTransformIn(lookups.In) class that overrides as_mysql/as_sqlite (wrapping placeholders with JSON_EXTRACT), as_oracle and split_parameter_list_as_sql (wrapping with JSON_VALUE/JSON_QUERY), leaves as_postgresql to the default behavior, and registers it on KeyTransform. This is exactly at the root-cause location (missing per-backend rhs JSON wrapping for the IN lookup) and mirrors the existing KeyTransformExact logic.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause by adding and registering the missing KeyTransformIn lookup; the reproduction and regression tests pass on SQLite (model_fields + queries: 792 tests OK) and __in now matches the exact lookup.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/functions/datetime.py, TruncDate.as_sql and TruncTime.as_sql unconditionally computed tzname via timezone.get_current_timezone_name(), ignoring the tzinfo passed to the expression.
summary.solution: The patch replaces the hardcoded 'timezone.get_current_timezone_name() if settings.USE_TZ else None' in both TruncDate.as_sql and TruncTime.as_sql with self.get_tzname(), the TimezoneMixin method that honors self.tzinfo and still returns None when USE_TZ is False. This matches the exact root cause and both affected code paths, and adds regression tests.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at both sibling locations using the intended mixin method; all 81 tests including the two new timezone tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/query.py the QuerySet.query setter only set self._query and never updated _iterable_class, so a values()/annotate() Query pickled and assigned to a fresh QuerySet still used ModelIterable, returning broken model instances instead of dicts and crashing with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'attname'.
summary.solution: The patch modifies the query.setter to set self._iterable_class = ValuesIterable when value.values_select is truthy. This changes the exact root-cause location (the query setter where the Query is assigned) so the QuerySet's iterable class is reconciled with the values-nature of the assigned query. It matches Django's accepted fix for this ticket.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location and all tests pass (queryset_pickle 37, queries+aggregation 470); the values_list-returns-dicts case is a known documented limitation, not a regression.

summary.problem: In django/core/files/locks.py, the posix lock() and unlock() functions compared fcntl.flock() result with `ret == 0`, but flock returns None on success (raising OSError on failure), so they always returned False.
summary.solution: The patch wraps fcntl.flock() in try/except: returns True on success and False on OSError, for both lock() and unlock(). This is exactly at the root-cause location and matches the fix I proposed and the one suggested in the issue.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly fixes the root cause; verified that success returns True, non-blocking lock contention returns False, and locks are released properly.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/query.py the QuerySet.ordered property returns True whenever default_ordering and Meta.ordering are set, ignoring that a GROUP BY query (from annotate with an aggregate) causes the SQL compiler to drop the ORDER BY clause.
summary.solution: The patch adds a check in the 'ordered' property: when the ordering would only come from Meta (default_ordering + Meta.ordering) but the query has a GROUP BY (self.query.group_by is not None), it returns False. This exactly mirrors the compiler logic in compiler.py (lines 588-591) where order_by is set to None for GROUP BY queries whose ordering originated only from _meta_ordering. It fixes the root cause at the point of creation of the wrong value.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct fix at the root-cause location; the new and existing tests (536 across queries/aggregation/annotations) all pass, and non-aggregate annotate (group_by stays None) is unaffected.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/expressions.py, SQLiteNumericMixin.as_sqlite wraps only the inner source expression (e.g. Lag) in CAST(... AS NUMERIC), so Window.as_sql then appends 'OVER (...)' outside the CAST, producing the invalid SQL 'CAST(LAG(...) AS NUMERIC) OVER (...)'.
summary.solution: The patch adds an as_sqlite() method to the Window class that, when the source expression is a DecimalField, compiles the source via source_expression.as_sql (bypassing SQLiteNumericMixin's inner CAST), builds the full 'expr OVER (window)' clause, and wraps the entire thing in CAST(... AS NUMERIC). This is at the exact root-cause location and produces valid SQL: CAST(LAG(...) OVER (...) AS NUMERIC). It matches the root cause I identified.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct fix at the root-cause location: the exact reported query now yields valid SQL and correct Decimal results, and all 53 window and 154 expressions tests pass. Only a minor maintainability concern (duplicated window-building logic).

defects.description: Window.as_sqlite duplicates the entire window-clause construction logic from Window.as_sql (partition_by/order_by/frame handling). If as_sql is later modified, as_sqlite can drift out of sync. A cleaner approach (as used in the official fix) is to copy the expression, set the inner source's output_field to FloatField, and delegate to a shared SQLiteNumericMixin/super().as_sqlite.
defects.suggestion: In expressions.py Window class, refactor as_sqlite to reuse as_sql instead of re-implementing the window-building logic, e.g. by copying source expressions and delegating cast wrapping to a shared mixin.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/admin/utils.py display_for_field(), JSONField values were rendered via field.get_prep_value() which calls json.dumps with default ensure_ascii=True, escaping non-ASCII (e.g. Chinese) chars to \uXXXX in the admin.
summary.solution: The patch changes display_for_field to use json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, cls=field.encoder) instead of get_prep_value, so unicode chars display as-is. It preserves the TypeError fallback to display_for_value and adds test cases for non-ASCII values. This is exactly the root-cause location and matches the accepted Django #13512 fix.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; all admin_utils, json field, and admin_views tests pass and unicode now displays correctly while the invalid-JSON fallback still works.

summary.problem: In django/core/management/base.py, OutputWrapper (a TextIOBase subclass) inherits a no-op flush() from TextIOBase, so its __getattr__ proxy never forwards flush() to self._out; management command output is not flushed until the end.
summary.solution: The patch adds an explicit flush() method to OutputWrapper that calls self._out.flush(). This targets the exact root cause: it overrides the inherited no-op flush so flushes are forwarded to the underlying stream, matching my proposed fix in both file and function.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of creation and passes verification and regression tests; approve.

summary.problem: django/contrib/auth/checks.py check_user_model raises auth.E003 whenever USERNAME_FIELD's field.unique is False, ignoring a total UniqueConstraint in Model._meta.constraints that enforces uniqueness.
summary.solution: The patch adds a check for a UniqueConstraint in cls._meta.constraints whose fields equal (USERNAME_FIELD,) and condition is None, and skips the E003 error and W004 warning in that case. This is exactly at the root-cause location (the branch that creates the error), and correctly restricts the exemption to single-field, unconditional constraints.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location and correctly handles edge cases (multi-field and conditional constraints still error); all existing and new tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/sql/query.py, Query.resolve_lookup_value reconstructs a namedtuple with type(value)(generator), but namedtuples require expanded positional args, causing TypeError: __new__() missing required positional argument.
summary.solution: The patch adds a branch in resolve_lookup_value: when value has _fields (a namedtuple), it reconstructs via type(value)(*generator), unpacking the resolved elements; plain lists/tuples keep the iterator-based construction. This changes the exact root-cause location where the wrong value is created, matching my proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the point of creation; all 553 expressions/queries tests pass including the added named-tuple range test, with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/utils/dateformat.py, DateFormat.y() used str(self.data.year)[2:], which for years < 1000 returns wrong/unpadded digits (e.g. year 123 -> '3').
summary.solution: The patch changes y() to return '%02d' % (self.data.year % 100), correctly taking the last two digits and zero-padding them. This is exactly the root-cause location and matches the reviewer's proposed fix. It also adds a regression test test_year_before_1000.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause directly and produces correct, consistent output for all tested years; all 18 tests pass including the new one.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/auth/forms.py, ReadOnlyPasswordHashField.__init__ did not set disabled=True by default, forcing forms (e.g. UserChangeForm) to implement a clean_password method to protect the password value; omitting it is a documented pitfall.
summary.solution: The patch adds kwargs.setdefault('disabled', True) in ReadOnlyPasswordHashField.__init__ (the root-cause point of creation), so tampered submissions are ignored in favor of initial data. It also removes the now-redundant clean_password method from UserChangeForm and updates the docs and release notes accordingly. This matches the intended fix exactly and is at the correct depth in the call stack.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix using setdefault (override-friendly, backward compatible); all 570 auth tests pass including test_bug_19133 which verifies password tampering is ignored.

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/operations/models.py, CreateModel.reduce()'s AlterModelOptions branch merged options with {**self.options, **operation.options} but never removed options absent from operation.options, so squashing AlterModelOptions(options={}) into CreateModel failed to clear model options.
summary.solution: The patch computes the merged options and then pops any key in AlterModelOptions.ALTER_OPTION_KEYS not present in operation.options, exactly mirroring AlterModelOptions.state_forwards(). This is at the exact root-cause location (the reduce() AlterModelOptions branch) and correctly clears removed options while preserving non-ALTER keys like 'proxy'.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix consistent with state_forwards semantics; all optimizer and full migrations tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/utils/functional.py the lazy proxy class (__proxy__) lacked a __radd__ method, so concatenating a real str/bytes on the left with a lazy string (str + __proxy__) raised TypeError, which the template add filter swallowed and returned ''.
summary.solution: The patch adds a __radd__ method to the lazy __proxy__ class that returns other + str(self) for text-delegating proxies, other + self.__bytes_cast() for bytes-delegating proxies, and NotImplemented otherwise. This is exactly at the root-cause location (the missing reflected-add operator on the lazy object), fixing the failure for all left-side str/bytes + lazy concatenations, not merely the add filter symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the true root cause at the point of creation (missing __radd__ on the lazy proxy), correctly delegates text/bytes and returns NotImplemented for other types; all reproduction and regression tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py check_constraints(), table/column identifiers are interpolated into PRAGMA foreign_key_check(%s), PRAGMA foreign_key_list(%s), and a SELECT without proper quoting, so SQL-keyword table names (e.g. 'order') raise sqlite3.OperationalError.
summary.solution: The patch wraps every interpolated identifier with self.ops.quote_name() at all three sites in the pragma branch and also replaces the hardcoded backticks in the fallback branch with quote_name(). This fixes the root cause (identifier interpolation), not just a single symptom path, and covers every code path in check_constraints. It also adds an Order/OrderItem model and a regression test using a reserved-keyword table name.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch matches the identified root cause exactly, quotes all identifiers in every affected code path, and all backends/fixtures tests (297) pass including the new reserved-keyword test.

summary.problem: Feature request: runserver command (django/core/management/commands/runserver.py) lacks a --skip-checks option to skip system checks for faster dev reloads.
summary.solution: The patch adds a --skip-checks argument to runserver's add_arguments and guards the check() call in inner_run behind 'if not options[skip_checks]'. This matches the intended root location. However, it ALSO moved self.check_migrations() inside the skip_checks guard, so --skip-checks additionally suppresses the migration-warning check.
summary.overall_assessment: Reject: --skip-checks in Django is defined to skip only system checks (as in BaseCommand.execute), not migration checks; the patch wrongly skips check_migrations() when skip_checks=True, diverging from intended semantics and failing the expected test.

defects.description: The patch places self.check_migrations() inside the 'if not options[skip_checks]:' block. This means running 'runserver --skip-checks' also skips the migration check and suppresses the 'You have N unapplied migration(s)' warning. Across Django, --skip-checks (BaseCommand.execute) only skips system checks; migration checks are controlled separately and still run. A test mirroring the intended behavior (mock check and check_migrations, call with skip_checks=True, assert check.assert_not_called() and check_migrations.assert_called()) fails because check_migrations is NOT called with this patch.
defects.suggestion: In runserver.py inner_run(), keep only the system checks under the guard and leave check_migrations() unconditional so migration warnings still display with --skip-checks.

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/loader.py, MigrationLoader.load_disk rejects any migrations module whose __file__ is None (line 93), which wrongly excludes regular packages in frozen environments that legitimately lack __file__; the namespace-package check should instead test whether __path__ is not a list.
summary.solution: The source hunk is correct: it reorders the checks (tests __path__ presence first) and replaces the bare __file__-is-None namespace check with `getattr(module,'__file__',None) is None and not isinstance(module.__path__, list)`, exactly matching the intended/official fix and the root cause. However, the patch's second hunk (tests/migrations/test_loader.py) is malformed: its hunk header (@@ -512,6 +512,32 @@) does not match the actual context/added line counts, so `git apply` fails with 'corrupt patch at line 62' (exit 128) and the whole patch cannot be applied.
summary.overall_assessment: The core logic fix is at the correct root-cause location and is functionally verified correct, but the delivered patch is corrupt and cannot be applied as-is, so it must be corrected before acceptance.

defects.description: The test hunk header '@@ -512,6 +512,32 @@' is inconsistent with the hunk body (only 4 context lines exist and the added-line count is wrong), causing `git apply` to abort with 'corrupt patch at line 62' (exit code 128). The patch cannot be applied at all in its delivered form.
defects.suggestion: Regenerate the diff so the test hunk header line counts match the actual context and added lines (e.g. correct the '-512,6 +512,32' counts), so the patch applies cleanly.

defects.description: The added test does not exercise MigrationLoader.load_disk() at all; it re-implements the namespace-detection boolean inline on a mock module and asserts on that copy. It provides no real regression protection for the patched code path.
defects.suggestion: Write a test that actually calls load_disk() (e.g. patch import_module to return a module with __file__=None and a list __path__) and assert the app is placed in migrated_apps, plus a namespace-package case asserting unmigrated_apps.

summary.problem: django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py check_sqlite_version() enforced only SQLite >= 3.8.3, so Django still supported SQLite versions below 3.9.0 despite the decision to drop them.
summary.solution: The patch raises the minimum required version in check_sqlite_version() to (3, 9, 0) with an updated error message, updates the matching test (tests/backends/sqlite/tests.py), and updates docs (databases.txt, GIS install matrix, 3.2 release notes). This targets exactly the root-cause location identified.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly fixes the root cause at the minimum-version gate and keeps the legitimate runtime JSON1 probe; the full sqlite backend test suite (32 tests) passes.

summary.problem: django/utils/autoreload.py get_child_arguments() detected `python -m django` only, by comparing sys.argv[0] to django.__main__.__file__, relying on __file__ and hardcoding the 'django' package.
summary.solution: The patch replaces the __file__-based comparison with the documented approach: it reads sys.modules['__main__'].__spec__.parent and, if truthy, emits ['-m', <parent>]. This correctly targets the root cause location/function and matches the intended fix, enabling autoreload for any `python -m <pkg>` launch. It also updates the TestChildArguments unit tests.
summary.overall_assessment: The source fix is correct and at the root cause, but the patch fails to update the pre-existing test RestartWithReloaderTests.test_python_m_django, which now raises RuntimeError, leaving the test suite failing.

defects.description: The pre-existing test RestartWithReloaderTests.test_python_m_django mocks the old detection mechanism (django.__main__.__file__ + sys.argv[0]) and does not set __main__.__spec__.parent. After the patch changes get_child_arguments() to use __main__.__spec__.parent, this test's mocked scenario no longer matches the -m branch and falls through to `elif not py_script.exists()`, raising RuntimeError('Script ... does not exist.'). Running `python tests/runtests.py utils_tests.test_autoreload` fails with 1 error.
defects.suggestion: Update RestartWithReloaderTests.test_python_m_django to set up a fake __main__ module whose __spec__.parent == 'django' (via mock.patch.dict('sys.modules', {'__main__': ...})) instead of mocking django.__main__.__file__, matching the new detection logic so the existing test passes.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/sql/compiler.py SQLInsertCompiler.execute_sql, values returned from INSERT (returning_fields such as the PK) are fetched from the cursor and returned raw, never passed through field converters (from_db_value / connection converters), so create()/bulk_create() set unconverted values on the model.
summary.solution: The patch modifies SQLInsertCompiler.execute_sql at the point of creation: instead of returning raw rows from each of the three fetch paths (bulk rows, fetch_returned_insert_columns, last_insert_id), it collects them into rows and applies converters via a small FieldAsExpression wrapper (exposing output_field and get_db_converters) fed into the existing get_converters/apply_converters infrastructure. This matches the root-cause location I identified and fixes all code paths, benefiting both save/_do_insert and bulk_create consumers.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point where raw DB values enter Python and reuses the standard converter machinery; all targeted and regression tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/core/servers/basehttp.py, ThreadedWSGIServer (via ThreadingMixIn) handles each request in a separate thread, and those per-request threads open database connections that are never closed, leaving lingering connections that cause 'database is being accessed by other users' at test DB teardown.
summary.solution: The patch overrides ThreadedWSGIServer.process_request_thread to call connections.close_all() in a finally block after each request, closing DB connections opened within the request thread. This is at the root-cause location (point of creation: the per-request worker thread) and matches the proposed fix in both file and function.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; the full servers test suite (including in-memory sqlite LiveServerDatabase tests that hit the DB over HTTP) passes with no regression.

defects.description: The added test uses unittest.mock to patch django.db.connections and only asserts close_all() was called, rather than verifying real connection-closing behavior in a request thread. It also carries trailing-whitespace warnings.
defects.suggestion: Prefer a test that exercises real DB connection closure (e.g., open a connection in a request thread and assert it is closed after process_request_thread), avoiding mocks.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py, HashedFilesMixin.post_process() yields every result from _post_process() on every pass, so the same original filename is yielded multiple times, inflating collectstatic stats and causing duplicate work in subclasses.
summary.solution: The patch modifies post_process() (the correct root-cause location) to stop yielding regular results during each pass (only propagating Exceptions immediately) and instead yields each file exactly once at the end by iterating over hashed_files. This correctly eliminates the duplicate yields, but it hardcodes processed=True for every yielded file instead of preserving the real processed status.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch is at the right location and fixes the duplicate-yield symptom, but it introduces a new correctness regression: files that were not actually post-processed (e.g. unchanged non-adjustable files on a second collectstatic run) are now reported as processed=True, producing wrong post-processed stats and log messages and misleading subclasses.

defects.description: The final loop 'for name in hashed_files: yield name, hashed_files[name], True' always emits processed=True. Verified via reproduction: on a second collectstatic run, a non-adjustable already-existing file (e.g. plain.js) originally yields processed=False (collectstatic logs 'Skipped post-processing' and excludes it from post_processed stats), but with the patch it yields processed=True and is falsely counted as post-processed. This is the exact stats-accuracy concern raised in the issue and also gives subclasses (WhiteNoise/S3) a wrong processed flag.
defects.suggestion: Preserve the real processed status per file (as the accepted Django fix does): yield non-adjustable files immediately with their actual (name, hashed_name, processed) during the first pass, accumulate adjustable files' final (name, hashed_name, processed) tuples in a dict updated across passes, and 'yield from' that dict at the end, instead of hardcoding processed=True for all entries in hashed_files.

summary.problem: django/utils/datastructures.py OrderedSet lacks a __reversed__ method, so reversed() raises TypeError despite the set being ordered.
summary.solution: The patch adds __reversed__ to OrderedSet returning reversed(self.dict), leveraging insertion-ordered dicts. This is exactly at the root cause (point of creation) and adds tests for populated and empty sets.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; reversed() now yields items in reverse insertion order and all 45 tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/query_utils.py, Q.deconstruct's single-child special case assumed the child was a (key, value) 2-tuple and did `kwargs = {child[0]: child[1]}`, crashing with TypeError for non-subscriptable children like Exists().
summary.solution: The patch guards the special case with `isinstance(child, tuple) and len(child) == 2`; otherwise it places the child into args as `(child,)`. This matches my proposed fix exactly, changing the root-cause location (Q.deconstruct, lines 88-90) at the point of value creation, and it adds regression tests.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly fixes the root cause in a backward-compatible way (kwargs behavior preserved for real field lookups) and all tests pass, so it should be approved.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/lookups.py, YearLookup.as_sql unconditionally applies the BETWEEN calendar-year optimization even when the underlying transform is ExtractIsoYear (lookup_name='iso_year'), producing wrong results since ISO year boundaries don't align with calendar year boundaries.
summary.solution: The patch adds a guard in YearLookup.as_sql that checks getattr(self.lhs, 'lookup_name', None) == 'iso_year' and falls back to super().as_sql() (EXTRACT-based SQL) for iso_year, while preserving the BETWEEN optimization for 'year'. This is at the exact root-cause location and fixes the optimization decision itself, not a downstream symptom. Tests are updated to split year/iso_year cases and add explicit iso_year lookup tests.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: iso_year lookups now generate EXTRACT SQL, year lookups still use BETWEEN, and the full test suite passes with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/__init__.py, AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__ used 'subclass in self._subclasses' which only matches the exact BigAutoField/SmallAutoField classes, so user-defined subclasses of them fail the AutoField subclass check and DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD raises ValueError.
summary.solution: The patch modifies AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__ to also return True when 'any(issubclass(subclass, cls) for cls in self._subclasses)', correctly accepting subclasses of BigAutoField and SmallAutoField. This is the exact root-cause location and logic; __instancecheck__ already handled subclass instances via isinstance. It also adds regression tests.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point where the flawed membership check is created, tests pass, and behavior is correct including negative cases.

summary.problem: In django/db/backends/postgresql/client.py settings_to_cmd_args_env(), env is initialized as {} and always returned, so with no passwd/service/ssl options it returns an empty dict instead of None; the base client's `if env:` then passes the empty dict to subprocess, discarding os.environ.
summary.solution: The patch changes `return args, env` to `return args, env or None`, so an empty env yields None (subprocess inherits os.environ) while a populated env is still merged. This fixes the root cause at the point of creation and aligns postgresql with the mysql/oracle/sqlite clients. Tests are updated to expect None.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct minimal fix at the root cause location; all dbshell tests pass and behavioral verification confirms None when empty and proper dict when env vars are set.

summary.problem: In django/core/validators.py URLValidator.__call__, URLs containing LF/CR/tab passed validation because on Python versions patched for bpo-43882 urlsplit() silently strips these characters before the URL is (re)validated, so ValidationError was never raised.
summary.solution: The patch adds an early guard in URLValidator.__call__ (right after the scheme check, before any urlsplit-based processing) that raises ValidationError if the value contains '\n', '\r', or '\t'. This is the point-of-creation fix and matches the issue's recommended approach of rejecting forbidden characters early.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; both previously-failing test cases now pass, LF/CR/tab are all rejected, and valid URLs still validate.

summary.problem: In django/utils/dateformat.py, DateFormat.Y() returned self.data.year as a raw int without zero-padding, so years < 1000 were not rendered as four digits.
summary.solution: The patch changes Y() to return '%04d' % self.data.year, zero-padding the year to at least four digits at the point of creation. This exactly matches the identified root cause and is consistent with the string-returning behavior of other format methods. A test covering years 4, 42, 476, 999 is also added.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; all existing dateformat and template date tests pass and manual verification confirms proper 4-digit padding without regressing normal years.

summary.problem: In django/db/backends/mysql/base.py, get_connection_params() passes deprecated mysqlclient kwargs 'db' and 'passwd'.
summary.solution: The patch renames kwargs['db'] to kwargs['database'] and kwargs['passwd'] to kwargs['password'] in get_connection_params(), matching the exact root cause location. Django requires mysqlclient >=1.4.0 (base.py line 36), which is above the 1.3.8 that introduced support for 'database'/'password', so the new kwargs are always accepted.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct minimal fix at the root cause; matches my proposed change exactly and is safe given Django's mysqlclient minimum version.

summary.problem: In django/db/backends/base/schema.py _create_unique_sql, a Table instance was passed to _index_columns/Columns where a table-name string is expected, so Columns.table was a Table object and references_column (self.table == table) always returned False.
summary.solution: The patch changes line 1254 to pass model._meta.db_table (a string) instead of the `table` Table object into _index_columns. This fixes the value at its point of creation, matching how _create_index_sql already calls _index_columns with a string. It matches my proposed root-cause fix exactly.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: references_column now returns True for the right table/column, generated SQL is unchanged/correct, and schema + migration test suites pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py, HashedFilesMixin.post_process references 'substitutions' at 'if substitutions:' but only assigns it inside the 'for i in range(self.max_post_process_passes)' loop, causing UnboundLocalError when max_post_process_passes = 0.
summary.solution: The patch initializes 'substitutions = False' immediately before the pass loop, ensuring the variable is always defined regardless of loop iterations. This matches the identified root cause exactly (point of creation, correct location and depth). It also adds a regression test with a MaxPostProcessPassesZeroStorage class.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly fixes the root cause; all storage tests (37) plus the new regression test pass and behavior is semantically correct (no spurious RuntimeError yielded).

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/executor.py, the squash-state maintenance logic in check_replacements() only records a replacement migration as applied when all replaced migrations are applied, but never records it as unapplied when the replaced set is unapplied; so unapplying replaced migrations leaves the squash migration marked applied.
summary.solution: The patch modifies check_replacements() to add the symmetric branch: if a replacement key is currently applied but its replaced set is no longer all-applied, it calls record_unapplied(*key). This is the canonical location where the squash migration's applied-state is created/maintained (mirror of the existing record_applied path), so it fixes the root cause rather than a symptom. Although I proposed fixing unapply_migration(), check_replacements() is the more complete location since it runs on every migrate and reconciles all paths including partial unapplies.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix that matches Django's canonical state-reconciliation logic; the added test fails without the source change and passes with it, and the full migrations suite (578 tests) passes.

summary.problem: In django/forms/boundfield.py, BoundWidget.id_for_label hardcoded 'id_%s_%s' % (name, index), ignoring the id available in self.data['attrs']['id'] and thus ignoring any custom auto_id or widget id set via ChoiceWidget.options.
summary.solution: The patch changes BoundWidget.id_for_label to return self.data['attrs'].get('id', 'id_%s_%s' % (name, index)). It fixes the exact root-cause location and depth, using the attrs id when present and falling back to the old format string when absent (backward compatible). It also adds two regression tests.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch targets the identified root cause directly, is backward compatible via the .get() fallback, and all tests pass; approve.

summary.problem: In django/utils/html.py trim_punctuation(), trailing punctuation trimming used index lengths from the unescaped string (len(stripped)/len(middle_unescaped)) to slice the escaped 'middle', so when HTML entities (e.g. &lt) were present the slice boundaries were wrong, duplicating characters like 'lt' into the trailing text.
summary.solution: The patch computes num_stripped = len(middle_unescaped) - len(stripped) (the count of trailing punctuation chars removed) and slices the escaped middle from the end using middle[-num_stripped:] and middle[:-num_stripped]. This matches my Step-3 proposal exactly and fixes the creation point of the wrong value (lines 286-287), not a downstream symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch targets the exact root-cause location and produces the expected output; all 53 related tests pass and manual regression checks are correct.

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/serializer.py, TypeSerializer.serialize() special-cased models.Model to the string 'models.Model' but returned an empty imports list, so migrations referencing models.Model in bases lacked 'from django.db import models', causing NameError.
summary.solution: The patch changes the special_cases entry from (models.Model, 'models.Model', []) to (models.Model, 'models.Model', ['from django.db import models']), so the required import is emitted whenever models.Model is serialized. This is exactly the root-cause location (point of creation), matching my independent proposal. It also adds regression tests.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct minimal fix at the root cause; all 580 migrations tests pass including the new regression tests.

summary.problem: In django/forms/formsets.py BaseFormSet.full_clean(), the _non_form_errors ErrorList was created via self.error_class() without an error_class argument, so FormSet non-form errors lacked a 'nonform' CSS class analogous to forms' 'nonfield'.
summary.solution: The patch changes both creation points in full_clean() (line 336 for the initial/management-form errors and line 383 for the clean()/min-max ValidationError path) to pass error_class='nonform', which ErrorList prefixes into its rendered class list. It also adds release-notes/docs entries and two tests. This matches the root cause exactly and covers all code paths that create _non_form_errors.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the point of creation for both non-form error paths; all 75 formset tests plus model_formsets pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/forms/forms.py, BaseForm._clean_fields() and changed_data accessed values via the unbound field (get_initial_for_field / _field_data_value) instead of the BoundField, so for disabled datetime fields _clean_fields() could return a value with microseconds while form[name].initial stripped them, causing divergence.
summary.solution: The patch adds BoundField._did_change() and BoundField._clean_value() to encapsulate the per-field logic, then rewrites _clean_fields() to use bf._clean_value()/bf.initial and changed_data to '[name for name in self.fields if self[name]._did_change()]'. This matches the root-cause location (routing value access through BoundField) proposed in Step 3; it uses self[name] instead of the issue's suggested _bound_items() helper, which is functionally equivalent.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause refactor: disabled-field cleaning now goes through BoundField.initial (with microsecond stripping) so cleaned_data matches form[name].initial, and all 936 form/model-form tests pass including the referenced test.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/reverse_related.py, ManyToManyRel.identity includes self.through_fields, which can be a list; since identity must be hashable (used by __hash__), a list value causes 'TypeError: unhashable type: list' during model checks.
summary.solution: The patch wraps self.through_fields in make_hashable() within ManyToManyRel.identity (line 313), exactly matching the root cause. It also adds a regression test model with list through_fields and a test asserting rel.identity is hashable for both tuple and list cases.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the exact point of creation (the identity tuple), and all m2m_through and relative-field tests pass, so it should be approved.

summary.problem: Feature request: model formsets (django/forms/models.py BaseModelFormSet.save_new_objects) had no reliable way to disallow creating new objects; users misused extra=0.
summary.solution: The patch adds an `edit_only` parameter to formset_factory, modelformset_factory, and inlineformset_factory, wires it onto the FormSet class, and in BaseModelFormSet.save_new_objects skips creating new objects when edit_only is True. It additionally adds a non-form ValidationError in BaseFormSet.full_clean when extra (non-empty) forms are submitted in edit_only mode. This matches the root-cause location (save_new_objects is exactly where new objects are created) and covers all factory paths (model, inline, and generic inline which delegates to modelformset_factory).
summary.overall_assessment: Correct, root-cause fix with defense-in-depth validation; edit_only defaults to False so existing behavior is unchanged and the full test suites pass.

defects.description: full_clean references self.edit_only, but edit_only is not declared as a class-level default on BaseFormSet/BaseModelFormSet; it is only supplied via the factory attrs dict. Formsets instantiated by directly subclassing BaseFormSet without the factory would raise AttributeError. However, this pattern is already unsupported (renderer, min_num, etc. also come from the factory), so no supported code path is affected. Behaviorally this patch also makes an edit_only formset invalid when new data is posted, whereas a purely silent-skip approach would keep it valid; both satisfy the requirement to disallow creation and defaults preserve backward compatibility.
defects.suggestion: Optionally add `edit_only = False` as a class attribute on BaseFormSet (and BaseModelFormSet) for robustness against direct subclassing.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/admin/views/autocomplete.py AutocompleteJsonView.get(), the result dict construction is inlined in the JsonResponse call, so customizing autocomplete result fields requires overriding the whole get() method.
summary.solution: The patch extracts the result-building logic into a new serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name) method returning {'id': ..., 'text': ...} and updates get() to call self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name) in the list comprehension. This exactly matches the requested extension point and the root-cause location, adding no behavior change for the default case.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch is a clean, minimal refactor at the correct location that adds the requested extension point without altering default behavior; tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/utils/autoreload.py, get_child_arguments() built the reloader child command with only -W warnoptions, omitting Python's -X options (sys._xoptions), so options like `-X utf8` were lost on reload.
summary.solution: The patch extends the args list in get_child_arguments() to also emit -X options from sys._xoptions, formatting each as '-Xkey' when the value is True and '-Xkey=value' otherwise. This is exactly at the root-cause location (the argument-construction line). It also updates existing tests to mock sys._xoptions and adds new tests for True and value cases.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location, handles both xoption formats, and all 83 autoreload tests pass plus real subprocess verification confirms -Xutf8/-Xdev propagation.

summary.problem: In the database backends' _prepare_tzname_delta() (django/db/backends/{postgresql,mysql,oracle}/operations.py), the code blindly flips the '+'/'-' sign across the whole tzname; since Django 3.2 timezone._get_timezone_name() returns full IANA names, 'Etc/GMT-10' is wrongly turned into 'Etc/GMT+10', reversing the UTC direction (UTC-10 instead of UTC+10).
summary.solution: The patch adds an early return `if tzname.startswith('Etc/GMT'): return tzname` in _prepare_tzname_delta() of all three backends, so IANA Etc/GMT names are passed through unchanged instead of having their sign flipped. This is exactly the root-cause location. Verified against a real PostgreSQL 14 instance: without the fix the ORM emits `AT TIME ZONE 'Etc/GMT+10'` (=> 2021-01-01 02:00, UTC-10, wrong), with the fix it emits `AT TIME ZONE 'Etc/GMT-10'` (=> 2021-01-01 22:00, UTC+10), which is identical to the desired Django 3.1 result for `-10`.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location for all three affected backends and produces the semantically correct result confirmed empirically against PostgreSQL; the full db_functions datetime test suite (88 tests) passes.

defects.description: The added regression test test_trunc_func_with_etc_gmt_timezone passes both WITH and WITHOUT the source fix, so it does not actually guard against the reported regression. It computes `expected` from Python's astimezone using the real tz, but the comparison does not detect the reversed-offset SQL that the bug produces. The behavioral difference was instead confirmed at the SQL/ORM level (AT TIME ZONE 'Etc/GMT+10' vs 'Etc/GMT-10').
defects.suggestion: Strengthen the test to assert the concrete truncated instant (e.g. compare model.truncated normalized to UTC against a hard-coded expected UTC datetime) or assert the generated SQL contains AT TIME ZONE 'Etc/GMT-10', so it fails when the sign flip is applied.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/admin/helpers.py AdminReadonlyField.get_admin_url, the reverse() call omitted current_app, so URLs for readonly ForeignKey fields always resolved to the default admin site (/admin/...) instead of the current custom admin site.
summary.solution: The patch adds current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name to the reverse() call in get_admin_url, exactly at the root cause. self.model_admin is set in the constructor and exposes admin_site.name, so the value is valid. It also adds a regression test using a custom admin site (admin2) plus registrations of ReadOnlyRelatedField and Language.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point where the wrong URL is created and follows the established current_app convention used elsewhere in the admin; all tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/forms/models.py, ModelChoiceIteratorValue defines __eq__ but not __hash__, so Python sets __hash__ to None making instances unhashable; using them as dict keys/lookups (e.g. `value in self.show_fields`) raises TypeError: unhashable type: 'ModelChoiceIteratorValue'.
summary.solution: The patch adds a __hash__ method to ModelChoiceIteratorValue returning hash(self.value). This is exactly the root-cause location and matches the Step 3 proposal. The hash is consistent with __eq__ (which compares self.value), so equal objects and value-equal scalars hash equally, allowing correct dict/set membership.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause by restoring hashability at the point of creation; the reported dict-lookup case now works, equality behavior is preserved, and model_forms tests pass (the only test errors are pre-existing environment import errors unrelated to the patch).

summary.problem: In django/contrib/admin/options.py ModelAdmin.get_search_results(), the loop calls queryset = queryset.filter(or_queries) once per search word, so for multi-valued relations (e.g. the reported reverse-FK clientoffice__name) every word adds another JOIN, causing the query to stall with many words.
summary.solution: The patch refactors get_search_results to collect per-word OR Q-objects and, when NO search field spans a multi-valued relation, combine them into a single filter() call; but when any field IS multi-valued (exactly the reported scenario), it keeps the original per-word filter() loop unchanged. Empirically the generated SQL for a multi-valued search is byte-for-byte identical to the original (same 8 JOINs for 4 words, identical MD5 hash), and the single-valued branch is a no-op because Django's ORM already reuses joins for non-multivalued relations across separate filter() calls.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch does not fix the root cause: the reported multi-valued-relation case still produces one JOIN per word (identical SQL to the unpatched code), so the performance bug remains; the added optimization only touches a case (single-valued) that never had extra joins.

defects.description: The reported bug concerns multi-valued relations (reverse FK / M2M such as clientoffice__name) where each search word adds a JOIN. The patch takes the spans_multi_valued branch for exactly these cases and preserves the original per-word queryset.filter() loop, so the number of JOINs still grows with the number of words. Verified: for search_fields=['name','members__name'] with 4 words, both original and patched code produce 8 JOINs and identical SQL (MD5 c8809aa22310485945b69425acc4096f). The performance problem described in the issue is therefore not fixed.
defects.suggestion: Combine the per-word OR queries into a single queryset.filter() call for the multi-valued case as well (e.g. queryset.filter(reduce(operator.and_, queries))), which is what actually collapses the repeated joins into one per relation; the single-valued-only branch does not change any SQL and is effectively dead optimization.

defects.description: The non-multi-valued branch that combines queries into a single filter() call produces the same SQL as the original code because Django's ORM already reuses joins for single-valued relations across separate filter() calls (verified: 1 JOIN in both original and patched). This branch adds complexity without changing behavior.
defects.suggestion: Remove the redundant branching and address the actual multi-valued join explosion instead.

summary.problem: In django/core/management/commands/inspectdb.py (handle_inspection, is_relation block), the generated ForeignKey ignored relations[column_name][0] (the referenced column), so a FK to a non-PK column like foo(other_id) was emitted as a plain FK defaulting to the PK.
summary.solution: The patch modifies the is_relation block in inspectdb.py to look up the referenced table's primary key via get_primary_key_column and, when the referenced column differs from that PK, adds extra_params['to_field']=<column>. It also fixes sqlite3 get_relations to parse the 'CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY(...)' syntax needed to introspect such FKs, and adds a passing regression test. This matches the identified root-cause location and depth exactly.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the point where the FK field is generated; new test passes and existing relation tests confirm PK-referencing FKs still omit to_field (no regression).

defects.description: For a self-referential FK (rel_to == 'self') that references a non-primary-key column, to_field is not emitted because the branch is skipped when rel_to == 'self'. This is a rare edge case not covered by the issue, but the behavior is technically incomplete.
defects.suggestion: In inspectdb.py, also compute rel_col/rel_pk for the self-referential case (use table_name as the referenced table) so to_field is emitted when appropriate.

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/autodetector.py, only_relation_agnostic_fields() uses `del deconstruction[2]['to']` which assumes 'to' is always in the deconstructed kwargs of a relation field; a custom ForeignKey that removes 'to' in its deconstruct() triggers KeyError.
summary.solution: The patch replaces `del deconstruction[2]['to']` with `deconstruction[2].pop('to', None)`, which removes 'to' when present and safely no-ops when absent. This is exactly the root-cause location and logic; it also adds a regression test reproducing the reported custom hardcoded-FK case.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the precise creation/use site, is semantically identical for the normal case, and the reproduction plus full autodetector suite (139 tests) pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/sql/query.py Query.combine builds change_map incrementally via self.join/table_alias, producing intersecting keys/values (e.g. {'T4':'T5','T5':'T6'}), which violates the disjoint assertion in Query.change_aliases and raises AssertionError for qs1 | qs2.
summary.solution: The patch modifies table_alias() to loop `while alias in self.alias_map` incrementing the numeric suffix. This only avoids collisions with aliases already present in self.alias_map; it does NOT prevent the change_map key/value intersection, because the conflicting rhs aliases (future change_map keys) are not in self.alias_map during combine. It does not touch the root-cause location (change_aliases / combine ordering).
summary.overall_assessment: Rejected: the exact scenario from the problem statement (qs1 | qs2) still raises AssertionError after applying the patch, so the reported bug is not fixed. The patch's own added test uses an unrelated School/Teacher scenario that does not reproduce the bug, giving false confidence.

defects.description: The added `while alias in self.alias_map` loop in table_alias() does not resolve the AssertionError. Reproducing the issue's exact code (qs1 | qs2 with Foo/Bar/Baz/Qux models) still raises AssertionError from change_aliases because change_map keys/values still intersect. The loop only guards against aliases already in self.alias_map, but the intersecting aliases are rhs aliases that are not yet in self.alias_map during Query.combine.
defects.suggestion: Fix the root cause in Query.change_aliases: handle intersecting change_map keys/values by relabeling in a safe order (e.g. detect keys that are also values and route them through temporary intermediate aliases), as in Django's official fix for ticket #15128. The change should live at the point where the relabeling occurs, not at table_alias.

defects.description: The added tests use School/Teacher models that do not reproduce the reported bug's alias arrangement, so they pass even though the bug is unfixed, providing false confidence.
defects.suggestion: Add a regression test that reproduces the exact reported scenario (nested reverse foreign keys producing sequential rhs aliases) and assert that both qs1 | qs2 and qs2 | qs1 succeed.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/expressions.py, public expression classes (Value, Func, When, Case, OrderBy, etc.) deconstructed to their full internal path 'django.db.models.expressions.X' because their @deconstructible decorator (inherited from Expression) had no explicit path, defaulting to obj.__class__.__module__.
summary.solution: The patch adds path='django.db.models.X' to the @deconstructible decorator on each publicly importable expression class (Expression, OuterRef, Func, Value, ExpressionList, ExpressionWrapper, When, Case, Subquery, Exists, OrderBy, Window, WindowFrame, RowRange, ValueRange), mirroring the existing treatment of F. This targets the exact root-cause location where the deconstruct path is produced.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location, produces the expected simplified paths, and correctly leaves non-exported subclasses (e.g. RawSQL) on the full path via the type(obj) is klass guard; all relevant test suites pass.

summary.problem: MigrationRecorder (django/db/migrations/recorder.py) methods ensure_schema/applied_migrations/record_applied/record_unapplied ignore the db_router's allow_migrate rules, so the django_migrations table is created and written on every connection regardless of the router.
summary.solution: The patch adds `router.allow_migrate(self.connection.alias, self.Migration._meta.app_label)` guards to ensure_schema, applied_migrations, record_applied, record_unapplied and flush. This is at the correct root-cause location. However the router check omits the `model_name` argument, and combined with the new test that drops a shared table, it breaks existing tests.
summary.overall_assessment: The source fix is in the right place but introduces regressions: existing test migrations.test_commands.MigrateTests.test_migrate_fake_initial fails (in isolation) and the patch's own added test drops the 'other' django_migrations table breaking 10 tests in migrations.test_multidb. Tests fail, so request_changes.

defects.description: router.allow_migrate is called without the model_name argument (only alias + app_label). Routers that key off model_name (e.g. tests/migrations/routers.py TestRouter, which returns a falsy None/False for the Migration model on non-default DBs) now block recording migration state on databases where migrations ARE actually applied. This regresses migrations.test_commands.MigrateTests.test_migrate_fake_initial, which passes on baseline but fails in isolation with the patch: applied_migrations() returns {} on 'other', the executor re-creates already-existing tables, raising OperationalError: table "migrations_tribble" already exists.
defects.suggestion: Either pass the Migration model name to allow_migrate, or (as in the accepted upstream fix) also update tests/migrations/routers.py / expectations so the Migration model's recording is consistent with how model tables are migrated.

defects.description: The added test MigrationRecorderTests.test_migration_recorder_respects_router executes raw `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS django_migrations` on the 'other' connection and, because the router now prevents recreation, never restores it. As a TransactionTestCase this DDL is not rolled back, so the dropped table persists. Subsequent tests in migrations.test_multidb (MultiDBOperationTests) fail in tearDown (test_base.py: migration_qs.filter(app='migrations').delete()) with OperationalError: no such table: django_migrations. Result: 10 previously-passing tests error out when the module is run in full.
defects.suggestion: Do not drop the shared test-database table without restoring it; use isolated fixtures/assertions that don't mutate persistent schema, or recreate the table in cleanup.

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/operations/models.py, AlterTogetherOptionOperation had no reduce() that allowed optimizing through a sibling AlterFooTogether op (e.g. AlterUniqueTogether across an intervening AlterIndexTogether), so interleaved consecutive AlterUnique/IndexTogether ops (4) were not collapsed into (2).
summary.solution: The patch adds AlterTogetherOptionOperation.reduce() which returns True (optimize-through) when the other op is an AlterTogetherOptionOperation on the same model but a different option_name, and returns [operation] to collapse two same-type ops on the same model, otherwise delegating to super(). This is exactly at the root-cause location and enables the optimizer's left/right reduction to merge interleaved operations.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location and depth; all 296 migration tests pass and manual verification confirms correct merging, no cross-model over-merge, and preserved DeleteModel optimization.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/__init__.py, Field.__hash__ included self.model._meta.app_label/model_name, so the hash changed once a field was assigned to a model (via contribute_to_class), breaking dict/set membership.
summary.solution: The patch reverts __hash__ to return hash(self.creation_counter), which is set at construction and never changes, making the hash immutable. It fixes the exact root-cause location (Field.__hash__) and also replaces the outdated test asserting mutable-hash behavior with a proper immutability test. __eq__ still compares creation_counter and model, preserving the equal-objects-equal-hashes contract.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; bug reproduction passes and 341 related tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/query.py bulk_update(), the check `if not isinstance(attr, Expression)` is too narrow: F() is not a subclass of Expression, so plain F('...') values get wrapped in Value() and serialized to their string repr (e.g. 'F(name)') instead of resolving to a column.
summary.solution: The patch replaces `isinstance(attr, Expression)` with `hasattr(attr, 'resolve_expression')` (duck typing), so F() and other resolvable expressions are passed through to When() unchanged rather than wrapped in Value(). This is exactly the fix suggested in the issue and matches the root-cause location precisely. It also adds a regression test test_plain_f_expression.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; all bulk_update, queries, and expressions tests pass (597+ tests) with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/autodetector.py, generate_renamed_fields() looked up the new model state via self.to_state.models[app_label, old_model_name], but to_state is keyed by the new (renamed) model name, causing KeyError when a model and field are renamed together.
summary.solution: The patch changes line 824 to use `model_name` (the new name) instead of `old_model_name` for the to_state lookup, while correctly keeping old_model_name for the from_state lookup. This is exactly the root-cause fix I proposed, at the correct location. It also adds a regression test test_rename_model_and_field_together.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the exact point where the wrong key was used; targeted and full autodetector test suites (141 tests) pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/operations/models.py, CreateModel.reduce() lacked a branch to absorb a following AlterModelManagers operation (it only handled AlterModelOptions), so CreateModel + AlterModelManagers was not optimized into a single CreateModel.
summary.solution: The patch adds an elif branch in CreateModel.reduce() checking isinstance(operation, AlterModelManagers) and matching name_lower, returning a new CreateModel with managers=operation.managers while preserving fields, options, and bases. This matches the exact root-cause location and mirrors the existing AlterModelOptions handling. Two tests were added covering the simple case and the attribute-preservation case.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location (CreateModel.reduce) using the correct new managers value, and all 655 migration tests pass including the 2 new optimizer tests.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/json.py, compile_json_path (used by HasKeyLookup.as_sql) converts numeric-string keys like '1111' into array-index syntax ([1111]) instead of object-key syntax (."1111"), so has_key/has_keys/has_any_keys lookups fail to match numeric object keys on SQLite/MySQL/Oracle.
summary.solution: The patch adds compile_json_path_to_be_quoted() which always quotes keys as object keys, and overrides as_sql in HasKey and HasKeys (HasAnyKeys inherits) so the final rhs key of a has_key path is treated as an object key while intermediate keys remain array-index-capable. It also updates KeyTransformIsNull's as_oracle/as_sqlite to preserve array-index semantics for key__isnull since those no longer route through the now-quoting HasKey. This fixes the identified root cause at the has_key path.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch targets the correct root cause (numeric-key path compilation for has_key lookups); reproduction of numeric has_key/has_keys/has_any_keys and nested keys now works, and full test suites pass.

defects.description: The as_sql method body is duplicated nearly verbatim into both HasKey and HasKeys rather than adjusting the shared HasKeyLookup.as_sql / compile_json_path. This is functionally correct but increases maintenance burden and risk of future divergence.
defects.suggestion: Consider consolidating the object-key handling in the base HasKeyLookup.as_sql (or a shared helper) instead of copying the method into two subclasses.

summary.problem: In django/db/backends/base/schema.py _field_should_be_altered(), 'choices' was not in the non_database_attrs list, so changing/adding choices was treated as a schema change, causing SQLite to rebuild the table.
summary.solution: The patch adds 'choices' to the non_database_attrs list so it is popped from both old/new field kwargs before comparison, making the alter a noop. This is exactly the root-cause location shared by all backends, so SQLite now generates no SQL, matching PostgreSQL behavior. A regression test asserting assertNumQueries(0) on SQLite is included.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; the new test passes and the full schema+migrations suites (832 tests) pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/sql/subqueries.py UpdateQuery.get_related_updates (and pre_sql_setup in compiler.py), related_updates to ancestor tables are filtered using the child model's PK values (related_ids). With multiple inheritance the secondary parent has an independent PK, so the UPDATE filters the wrong rows, corrupting unrelated parent rows and failing to update the child's own parent rows.
summary.solution: The patch modifies get_related_updates: for each ancestor model it looks up self.model._meta.parents.get(model) and, when found, builds a subquery selecting the parent link field's attname from the child table filtered by the child PK, then filters the ancestor UpdateQuery with pk__in=subquery. This addresses the reported direct-parent case (its included tests pass), but _meta.parents only contains DIRECT parents.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the fix is incomplete. For multi-level inheritance where the field owner is a NON-direct grandparent reached through a secondary branch with an independent PK, parents.get(model) returns None and the code falls back to the original buggy behavior, silently failing to update and still able to corrupt rows.

defects.description: get_related_updates uses self.model._meta.parents.get(model), which only maps DIRECT parents. When an updated field is owned by a non-direct ancestor reached via a secondary inheritance branch with an independent primary key (e.g. class Top(pk); class Mid(Top); class Base(pk); class Child(Base, Mid) updating a Top-owned field), parent_link_field is None and the code falls back to query.add_filter('pk__in', self.related_ids) using the child's PK chain. This is exactly the original bug: verified in testbed that DeepMultiChild.objects.update(field_top=55) left the child rows unchanged ([0,1] instead of [55,55]). The correct approach collects per-parent-link PK values for every related-update model in pre_sql_setup at arbitrary depth.
defects.suggestion: Fix the point of creation in SQLUpdateCompiler.pre_sql_setup (compiler.py): make related_ids a dict keyed by model and add each related-update model's parent-link pk field to the pre-select query so correct per-parent PK values are captured for any inheritance depth; then filter each ancestor query with related_ids[model]. Do not rely on _meta.parents which only lists direct parents.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/query_utils.py, RegisterLookupMixin._unregister_lookup deletes the lookup from class_lookups but never calls cls._clear_cached_lookups(), leaving get_lookups' lru_cache stale.
summary.solution: The patch adds cls._clear_cached_lookups() after the del in _unregister_lookup, mirroring register_lookup. It also updates schema.tests test_func_unique_constraint_lookups to move the constraint assertions inside the register_lookup context manager, since after the fix the lookups are removed from the cache once the context exits. This exactly matches the root cause location and my proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location and includes the required accompanying test change; all schema and lookup tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/related.py ForeignKey.db_parameters (and the related-field alter loop in django/db/backends/base/schema.py _alter_field), the collation of a target primary key was not propagated to referencing FK columns, so MODIFY statements for FK columns omitted COLLATE and MySQL ADD CONSTRAINT failed.
summary.solution: The patch fixes the root cause by making ForeignKey.db_parameters propagate the target field's collation, and updates the alter paths: base schema _alter_field now triggers FK drop/recreate and emits _alter_column_collation_sql when the collation changes; MySQL adds an _alter_column_collation_sql override preserving null status; SQLite propagates the collation to remade FK tables. This matches the identified root cause (point of creation in ForeignKey.db_parameters) plus the downstream alter propagation.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the bug at its root (FK collation inheritance) and passes all relevant test suites with no regressions, so it is approved.

defects.description: The SQLite _remake_table override monkeypatches field.db_parameters via a per-field closure on a deepcopied body to inject collation. This works and is isolated to the remade table copy, but is a hacky mechanism compared to the cleaner db_parameters propagation used elsewhere.
defects.suggestion: Consider relying on the existing ForeignKey.db_parameters collation propagation rather than dynamically overriding db_parameters, to reduce complexity in _remake_table.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/manager.py, _get_queryset_methods.create_method manually copies only __name__ and __doc__ onto the generated manager_method, so inspect.signature reports manager_method's own (*args, **kwargs) instead of the wrapped queryset method's real signature.
summary.solution: The patch imports functools and decorates manager_method with @functools.wraps(method), removing the manual __name__/__doc__ assignments. functools.wraps copies full metadata including __wrapped__, which lets inspect.signature follow through to the original queryset method's signature. This matches the root-cause fix proposed in Step 3 exactly.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the point of method creation; bulk_create now reports (objs, batch_size=None, ...) and name/doc are preserved, with all manager/basic tests passing.

summary.problem: In django/utils/formats.py get_format(), a lazy string format_type causes TypeError because getattr()/cache_key require a real str, not a lazy proxy.
summary.solution: The patch adds 'format_type = str(format_type)' at the start of get_format(), coercing the lazy proxy to a real string before it is used in getattr() and the cache key. This is exactly the root-cause fix I proposed, at the point of creation/use of the wrong value.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; the reported repro (some_date|date:_('Y-m-d')) now works and all 36 relevant tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/sql/query.py Query.deferred_to_data(), `opts = cur_model._meta` uses a proxy model's meta when following a relation to a proxy model, so the concrete pk is not added to must_include, causing RelatedPopulator to fail with ValueError: 'id' is not in list for select_related().only() on proxy models.
summary.solution: The patch inserts `cur_model = cur_model._meta.concrete_model` before `opts = cur_model._meta`, so both `cur_model` (used as key in must_include) and `opts.pk` refer to the concrete model. This is functionally equivalent to (and slightly cleaner than) the fix suggested in the issue and targets the exact root-cause location I identified.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct file/function/line, adds valid regression tests, and all proxy_models plus defer/select_related/queries suites pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/template/defaultfilters.py floatformat(), line 154-155 used Decimal(repr(text)); for Decimal inputs repr() yields "Decimal('...')" which raises InvalidOperation and falls back to Decimal(str(float(text))), losing precision.
summary.solution: The patch adds an isinstance(text, Decimal) check at the point of creation: if text is already a Decimal it is used directly (d = text), otherwise the original Decimal(repr(text)) path is kept. This matches the identified root cause exactly and fixes precision at the source rather than masking a symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; the reported MWE now returns 42.12345678901234567890 and all 11 existing/added floatformat tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/forms/models.py, modelform_factory forced 'formfield_callback': None into form_class_attrs, and ModelFormMetaclass popped that None (line 266) so the base form's Meta.formfield_callback was overwritten with None; the factory-generated form ignored the inherited callback.
summary.solution: The patch stores formfield_callback in ModelFormOptions, makes the metaclass fall back to the base class/Meta callback and prefer opts.formfield_callback (from Meta) when present, propagates it onto the new class for inheritance, and changes modelform_factory to only add formfield_callback to form_class_attrs when it is truthy (no longer forcing None). This matches the root-cause locations I identified (metaclass line ~266 and factory line ~639).
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at both creation points; the exact issue scenario now yields required fields with 4 callback invocations, and the full model_forms/model_formsets/admin_widgets suites pass.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py, the get_prefetch_queryset methods (and GenericRelation's) call queryset.filter(**query) on the user-supplied Prefetch queryset; when that queryset is sliced (e.g. [:3]), filter() raises 'Cannot filter a query once a slice has been taken.'
summary.solution: The patch touches the correct locations (ForwardManyToOne, ReverseOneToOne, reverse many-to-one, M2M, and GenericRelation get_prefetch_queryset). For sliced querysets it saves low_mark/high_mark, calls query.clear_limits(), applies the __in filter across ALL instances, then re-applies the slice via set_limits(). This is semantically wrong: the LIMIT is applied to the single combined cross-instance query, so it returns a global slice of N rows total rather than N rows per parent instance.
summary.overall_assessment: Reject: the patch avoids the crash but produces incorrect prefetch results (a global slice instead of a per-instance slice), a high-severity correctness defect. The proper fix requires per-partition limiting (e.g. window functions / RowNumber), as done in Django's actual resolution.
