defects.description: For a reverse FK prefetch with a sliced queryset (Prefetch('rooms', queryset=Room.objects.all()[:3])), the patch clears limits, filters house__in=[all houses], then re-applies LIMIT 3 to the whole combined query. Verified empirically: with 2 houses of 5 rooms each, result was {'h1': 3, 'h2': 0} instead of the correct {'h1': 3, 'h2': 3}. The slice is applied globally, not per parent instance, giving incorrect prefetch results.
defects.suggestion: Do not naively re-apply low/high marks to the cross-instance query. Implement per-partition limiting using window functions (e.g. RowNumber partitioned by the relation) so each parent instance receives its own sliced subset, matching Django's actual fix for this ticket.

defects.description: Same global-slice defect for many-to-many prefetch: clear_limits then filter across all instances then set_limits applies one LIMIT to the entire query rather than per instance.
defects.suggestion: Apply per-partition slicing (window function) rather than re-applying limits to the combined query.

defects.description: The added tests only assert len(...) <= 3, which passes even when a parent instance receives 0 objects, so they fail to catch the global-slice bug and give a false sense of correctness.
defects.suggestion: Assert the exact per-instance count (e.g. each house gets exactly 3) to detect incorrect global slicing.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/expressions.py, the _connector_combinations 'operands of different type' block omitted Combinable.MOD from its connector tuple, so mixed Decimal/Integer (or Integer/Float) operands with MOD failed to resolve output_field to Decimal/Float.
summary.solution: The patch adds Combinable.MOD to the different-type numeric connector tuple (line ~536), enabling _resolve_combined_type to return DecimalField/FloatField for mixed-type MOD. It also updates the CombinedExpressionTests to include MOD in the tested connectors. This is exactly the root-cause location and matches my proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct minimal fix at the root cause; verified mixed-type MOD now resolves to Decimal/Float and same-type behavior is unchanged, with all tests passing.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/admin/options.py, ModelAdmin.changelist_view saves list_editable bulk edits (save_form/save_model/save_related/log_change loop) without a database transaction, so a mid-loop error leaves the DB in a partial/inconsistent state.
summary.solution: The patch wraps the save loop inside `with transaction.atomic(using=router.db_for_write(self.model)):`, matching the pattern already used by changeform_view and delete_view. This is exactly at the root-cause location (point where the writes occur). The changecount success-message block correctly stays outside the atomic block, and the required transaction/router imports already exist.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly fixes the root cause by adding transactional integrity around list_editable processing; all admin_changelist and admin_views tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py handle(), when changes are detected it always calls write_migration_files() and only afterward exits for --check, so makemigrations --check writes migration files instead of just exiting like migrate --check.
summary.solution: The patch moves the check_changes sys.exit(1) to BEFORE both write_migration_files() and write_to_last_migration_files(), and adds an informative log line. This fixes the point of creation so no migration files are written under --check (including --update --check). It matches the root cause location and depth identified independently.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix covering all output paths; full test suite (63 tests) and new no-files-created/update-check tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/views/generic/base.py, View.http_method_not_allowed() always returned a plain HttpResponseNotAllowed; for async views (view_is_async True) the view callable is marked as a coroutine, so ASGI awaits dispatch's result, causing 'object HttpResponseNotAllowed can't be used in await expression'.
summary.solution: The patch wraps the HttpResponseNotAllowed in an async func() and returns the coroutine when self.view_is_async (mirroring the existing options() implementation), and returns the response directly otherwise. This is exactly the root cause location and matches the fix I proposed.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; async views now return an awaitable 405 while sync views are unchanged, and all 66 async/generic view tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/core/management/commands/runserver.py handle(), the address '0' (parsed as an FQDN by naiveip_re) was used verbatim, so the startup message showed 'http://0:8000/' instead of the documented '0.0.0.0' shortcut.
summary.solution: The patch adds an elif branch in handle() that normalizes self.addr from '0' to '0.0.0.0' right after parsing, at the point where the address is created. This matches the root cause exactly, and it also adds a regression test test_runner_zero_address in tests/admin_scripts/tests.py.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the point of address creation with a proper test; all runserver tests pass and other address forms are unaffected.

summary.problem: Related managers unintentionally inherit the QuerySet's async acreate()/aget_or_create()/aupdate_or_create() methods, which call the QuerySet versions and bypass the related manager's sync logic (FK/M2M/generic setup). Root cause spans related_descriptors.py (RelatedManager, ManyRelatedManager) AND contenttypes/fields.py (GenericRelatedObjectManager), all of which override create/get_or_create/update_or_create.
summary.solution: The patch adds proper async acreate/aget_or_create/aupdate_or_create methods (wrapping each manager's own sync method via sync_to_async) to RelatedManager (reverse FK) and ManyRelatedManager (M2M) in related_descriptors.py, plus the sync_to_async import and new tests. This correctly fixes those two managers. However it does NOT add these async methods to GenericRelatedObjectManager in django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py, which has the identical bug and identical create/get_or_create/update_or_create overrides.
summary.overall_assessment: Incomplete fix: a sibling code path (generic relations manager) with the exact same root cause is left unpatched, verified to still raise SynchronousOnlyOperation on await animal.tags.acreate(...).

defects.description: GenericRelatedObjectManager overrides create(), get_or_create(), and update_or_create() (setting content_type/object_id) but has no acreate/aget_or_create/aupdate_or_create. It therefore still inherits the QuerySet async methods, which bypass this logic. Verified after applying the patch: `await animal.tags.acreate(tag=...)` raises django.core.exceptions.SynchronousOnlyOperation instead of creating a properly-linked object. This is the same root-cause bug in a sibling code path left unfixed.
defects.suggestion: Add async acreate/aget_or_create/aupdate_or_create methods to GenericRelatedObjectManager in django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py, each wrapping the manager's own sync create/get_or_create/update_or_create via sync_to_async (with matching signatures and .alters_data = True), and import sync_to_async there.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/sql/compiler.py SQLInsertCompiler.as_sql, raw field names (self.query.update_fields/unique_fields) were passed to on_conflict_suffix_sql, which quotes them directly as SQL identifiers, ignoring db_column and producing invalid ON CONFLICT SQL.
summary.solution: The patch resolves field names to their db_column via opts.get_field(name).column in the compiler before passing them to on_conflict_suffix_sql (with an empty-tuple fallback). This is exactly the root-cause location where the SQL arguments are constructed, and it fixes all backends (postgresql, mysql, sqlite) at once since they all quote the strings they receive.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location, matches the intended behavior (uses db_column names), and all existing tests plus a new custom-db_column regression test pass.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/auth/forms.py, UserCreationForm.save() overrides ModelForm.save() but never invokes m2m saving, so ManyToMany form field data is discarded.
summary.solution: The patch modifies UserCreationForm.save() to replicate ModelForm.save()'s m2m logic: when commit=True it calls self._save_m2m() after user.save(), and when commit=False it assigns self.save_m2m = self._save_m2m for deferred saving. This matches the root cause location and Django's canonical behavior exactly.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the exact function identified; mirrors ModelForm.save() semantics for both commit=True and commit=False and all 89 auth form tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/utils/timesince.py timesince(), the 'pivot' datetime (lines 93-100) was constructed without tzinfo, making it offset-naive; subtracting it from an aware 'now' at line 103 raised TypeError.
summary.solution: The patch adds tzinfo=d.tzinfo to the datetime.datetime(...) pivot construction so the pivot carries d's timezone. This is exactly the root-cause fix at the point where the wrong (naive) value was created, not a downstream guard. It also adds the reproducing test test_long_interval_with_tz.
summary.overall_assessment: Approve: the patch fixes the root cause at the correct location, all 18 tests pass, and both aware and naive datetimes now return '1\xa0month' correctly.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/files.py, FileField.deconstruct checks `if self.storage is not default_storage` using the evaluated storage, so a callable that returns default_storage wrongly omits the storage kwarg.
summary.solution: The patch changes deconstruct to first check `hasattr(self, '_storage_callable')` and, if present, always emit the original callable; otherwise it falls back to the previous `self.storage is not default_storage` check. This targets the exact root-cause location and preserves the reference to the callable regardless of its evaluated return value.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the point of creation of the deconstruct output; matches the proposed fix and passes all tests including new regression tests.

summary.problem: In django/core/servers/basehttp.py, the wsgiref-based ServerHandler used by runserver writes the full response body regardless of REQUEST_METHOD, so HEAD requests return a body (non-compliant with RFC 2616/9112) after body-stripping was removed from Django in #26052.
summary.solution: The patch overrides ServerHandler.finish_response() to, on HEAD requests, consume/close the response iterator, send only the headers (via send_headers if not already sent), and close the connection without writing body bytes; non-HEAD requests fall through to the parent implementation. This is at the exact root-cause location (runserver's ServerHandler, the point where output is produced) and matches the proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: HEAD returns headers only with Content-Length preserved while GET is unaffected; all servers/builtin_server tests pass and an end-to-end raw-socket test confirms empty HEAD body and intact GET body.

summary.problem: Feature request in django/db/models/constraints.py BaseConstraint: no way to customize the 'code' of the ValidationError raised by constraint.validate() (only the message was customizable).
summary.solution: The patch adds a new 'violation_error_code' parameter/attribute to BaseConstraint, CheckConstraint, UniqueConstraint and the postgres ExclusionConstraint, stores it, threads it through deconstruct()/__eq__/__repr__, and passes code=self.violation_error_code to every ValidationError raise site in validate(). This matches the root cause: the fix is at both the point of creation (__init__) and the points of use (raise sites).
summary.overall_assessment: Correct, complete implementation of the requested feature across all constraint classes; all 93 constraint/validation tests pass and manual verification confirms the code propagates to ValidationError and deconstruct/clone/eq behave correctly.

summary.problem: In django/forms/formsets.py, BaseFormSet.add_fields() compares 'index < initial_form_count' at line 493 without guarding against index being None, so empty_form (index=None) with can_delete=True and can_delete_extra=False raises TypeError.
summary.solution: The patch changes line 493 to 'self.can_delete and (self.can_delete_extra or (index is not None and index < initial_form_count))', adding a None guard identical to the pattern already used for the ordering field above it. This is exactly the root-cause location and mirrors the existing correct code.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the exact location; empty_form now renders without error while initial/extra form DELETE-field semantics are preserved, and the full formset test suite (159 tests) passes.

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/operations/fields.py, AlterField.reduce did not handle the case where the following operation is another AlterField on the same field, so consecutive AlterFields were never optimized.
summary.solution: The patch adds an elif branch in AlterField.reduce: if operation is an AlterField and is_same_field_operation(operation) is true, return [operation], letting the later AlterField absorb the earlier one. This is exactly the root-cause location and matches the fix suggested in the issue. It also adds two regression tests.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; reproduction and the full migrations test suite (714 tests) pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/auth/base_user.py, AbstractBaseUser.get_session_auth_hash() computes the HMAC using only settings.SECRET_KEY (via salted_hmac's default), so after rotating SECRET_KEY (with the old key placed in SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS), session verification in django/contrib/auth/__init__.py get_user() fails and all users are logged out.
summary.solution: The patch adds an optional `secret` parameter to get_session_auth_hash() and forwards it to salted_hmac, and updates get_user() to iterate over [SECRET_KEY, *SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS], verifying the stored session hash against each until a match is found. This directly addresses the root cause (hash creation tied only to SECRET_KEY) at the correct location and depth. New session creation and update_session_auth_hash still use the current SECRET_KEY, which is correct.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause exactly, is backward compatible (secret defaults to None -> SECRET_KEY), and all auth/session/crypto tests plus the new fallback tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/forms/widgets.py, SelectDateWidget.value_from_datadict only catches ValueError around datetime.date(int(y), int(m), int(d)), so a huge user-supplied year/month/day raises an uncaught OverflowError, crashing form validation.
summary.solution: The patch changes 'except ValueError:' to 'except (ValueError, OverflowError):' at the exact root-cause location, so oversized integers fall through to the pseudo-ISO fallback string and are later rejected as an invalid date. It also adds a regression test covering large year/month/day values.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of creation and matches the proposed fix; all tests pass and the reported crash is replaced by a clean 'Enter a valid date.' validation error while valid dates still work.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/fields/files.py, ImageField.contribute_to_class unconditionally connects the update_dimension_fields handler to the post_init signal (only checking cls._meta.abstract), causing a per-instance no-op signal overhead even when width_field and height_field are both unset.
summary.solution: The patch adds `and (self.width_field or self.height_field)` to the connect condition, so the post_init handler is only connected when at least one dimension field is configured. This is exactly at the root-cause location (point of creation/connection) and matches the fix I independently proposed.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the right depth; the no-op signal is no longer connected when unnecessary, and all dimension-update behavior is preserved via the still-present in-method guard and the descriptor __set__ direct-call path.

summary.problem: django/db/migrations/operations/models.py: AddIndex/RemoveIndex lacked a reduce() method, so the optimizer could not collapse redundant index add/remove operations.
summary.solution: The patch adds reduce() to both AddIndex and RemoveIndex, plus a references_model() override and a can_reduce_through() helper on IndexOperation. AddIndex followed by RemoveIndex of the same name correctly reduces to []. However it ALSO makes RemoveIndex followed by AddIndex of the same name reduce to [], which is semantically incorrect. It matches the root-cause location but introduces an incorrect optimization.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the RemoveIndex->AddIndex reduction can silently drop a legitimate index redefinition, producing an incorrect final migration state (high-severity correctness bug).

defects.description: RemoveIndex.reduce() returns [] when followed by an AddIndex with the same index name. This is incorrect: RemoveIndex only references a name, while the subsequent AddIndex may create a DIFFERENT index definition. Verified: RemoveIndex('Pony','idx') + AddIndex('Pony', Index(fields=['weight'], name='idx')) optimizes to [], dropping the index redefinition and leaving the pre-existing old index in place, contradicting the target state. Only AddIndex->RemoveIndex is safe to cancel; RemoveIndex->AddIndex is not.
defects.suggestion: Remove the reduce() override on RemoveIndex (and its can_reduce_through helper). Keep only AddIndex.reduce() reducing AddIndex followed by RemoveIndex of the same name to [], mirroring the upstream Django fix.

defects.description: Overriding references_model() on IndexOperation narrows the previously conservative base behavior (returns True) for ALL index operations, including RenameIndex which was not the target of this change. This alters optimizer reordering safety semantics beyond the scope of the fix and may permit unsafe reordering.
defects.suggestion: Avoid adding references_model()/can_reduce_through() to IndexOperation; the minimal fix only needs AddIndex.reduce() to detect a following same-name RemoveIndex.

summary.problem: Feature request: add a new template filter `escapeseq` in django/template/defaultfilters.py that escapes each element of a sequence individually (analogous to how `safeseq` relates to `safe`), for use with filters like `join` especially when autoescape is off.
summary.solution: The patch adds an `escapeseq` filter directly after `safeseq` in defaultfilters.py, returning `[conditional_escape(obj) for obj in value]`. This matches the identified location and correct approach exactly. It also adds documentation in docs/ref/templates/builtins.txt and unit tests covering both autoescape-on and autoescape-off cases.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly implements the requested feature at the right location with correct escaping semantics (no double-escaping), passes all tests, and introduces no regressions.

summary.problem: In django/contrib/admin/checks.py, BaseModelAdminChecks._check_readonly_fields_item builds the admin.E035 error message referencing only the index label 'readonly_fields[n]' and omits the offending field name, unlike other checks.
summary.solution: The patch modifies the admin.E035 Error message to the 'The value of %s refers to %s, which is not a callable...' form, passing field_name into the format args. This changes exactly the root-cause location (_check_readonly_fields_item message construction) and mirrors the wording of other checks like list_display/list_editable. It also updates the two existing tests to expect the new message.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location, is consistent with sibling checks, and all admin_checks (56) and modeladmin (168) tests pass.

defects.description: The documentation for admin.E035 still describes the old message wording ('The value of readonly_fields[n] is not a callable...') and was not updated to include the field name.
defects.suggestion: Update docs/ref/checks.txt admin.E035 entry to match the new 'refers to' wording for consistency.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/sql/where.py WhereNode.as_sql, the XOR fallback for databases lacking native XOR built SQL as (a OR b OR ...) AND (a+b+...) == 1, implementing 'exactly one true' instead of parity (odd count true).
summary.solution: The patch changes rhs = Exact(1, rhs_sum) to rhs = Exact(1, Mod(rhs_sum, 2)) (importing Mod), producing (a+b+...) % 2 == 1. This matches the root cause exactly: the point where the wrong comparison is created. Confirmed generated SQL now emits '1 = MOD(sum, 2)'.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct fix at the root cause; all xor_lookups tests plus new parity tests pass (1,0,1,0,1 semantics verified). Approve.

defects.description: New test file has trailing whitespace on several lines and no final newline; purely cosmetic and does not affect behavior.
defects.suggestion: Strip trailing whitespace and add a trailing newline (or fold these cases into the existing tests/xor_lookups/tests.py).

summary.problem: In django/forms/models.py BaseInlineFormSet.add_fields, when adding a new parent object whose FK target (to_field) has a default (e.g. a non-editable UUIDField), the code unconditionally did setattr(self.instance, to_field.attname, None). For a non-editable field the default value is only applied at Model.__init__ and is NOT regenerated on save(), so clearing it left the parent's id as None, saved as NULL and breaking the inline FK.
summary.solution: The patch modifies add_fields to only clear (set to None) the field value when the to_field is editable (so it can be re-submitted/regenerated on save), and for non-editable fields it preserves the default that was set at init while forcing the form field's initial to None via kwargs['initial']=None. InlineForeignKeyField.__init__ is updated to respect an explicitly-provided initial. This targets the exact root-cause location (add_fields) identified before reading the patch.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point where the value was wrongly nulled, preserves the previous editable-default behavior, and all relevant test suites pass including a new reproduction test.

summary.problem: In django/apps/registry.py, Apps.clear_cache() only cleared self.get_models cache and omitted the @functools.cache-decorated get_swappable_settings_name, so its cache persisted despite the docstring promising all internal caches are cleared.
summary.solution: The patch adds self.get_swappable_settings_name.cache_clear() to clear_cache(), directly at the root-cause location. This matches the fix proposed independently before reading the patch. It also adds three regression tests verifying both caches are cleared and that clear_cache() is idempotent.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause exactly and all 46 apps tests (including 3 new ones) pass; approve.

summary.problem: In django/db/models/sql/query.py get_aggregation(), the decision to use a subquery did not account for annotations containing window functions (contains_over_clause), so aggregating over a Window annotation produced SUM(window()) at the same query level, causing PostgreSQL GroupingError.
summary.solution: The patch adds a has_over_clause check that inspects self.annotations for contains_over_clause and adds it to the condition that forces the AggregateQuery subquery. This matches the identified root cause exactly: the window annotation is now pushed to the inner query and the aggregate references it via a Ref in the outer query. Verified generated SQL: 'SELECT SUM("__col1"), SUM("cumul") FROM (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(...) OVER (...), 0.0) AS "cumul", ... ) subquery'.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location and depth; all 734 tests across aggregation/window/queries suites pass and generated SQL correctly wraps the window function in a subquery.

defects.description: The added test has a trailing-whitespace line (git apply reported a whitespace warning). Purely cosmetic, no behavior impact.
defects.suggestion: Remove trailing whitespace on the blank line inside test_aggregate_over_window_function.

summary.problem: In django/db/migrations/serializer.py, FunctionTypeSerializer.serialize used klass.__name__ for classmethods bound to a class, dropping enclosing class names for nested classes (e.g. Profile.Capability serialized as just Capability).
summary.solution: The patch changes klass.__name__ to klass.__qualname__ at line 171, the exact root-cause location, so nested classes serialize with their full dotted path. It also adds a regression test for nested-class classmethod serialization. This matches my proposed fix precisely.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: nested classmethods now serialize to the full qualified path while top-level classes remain unchanged; all 54 writer tests pass.

summary.problem: In django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py handle(), the consistency-check comprehension used apps.get_models(app_label); since get_models's first positional arg is include_auto_created, the app_label was misinterpreted and ALL project models were returned, pairing every app_label with every model and passing invalid (app_label, model) combos to router.allow_migrate().
summary.solution: The patch replaces apps.get_models(app_label) with apps.get_app_config(app_label).get_models(), so each app_label is paired only with that app's own models. This is exactly the root-cause location (point where the wrong model set is created), not a downstream guard, and matches the intended fix.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location with a minimal change; the full migrations test suite (424 tests) and the routers consistency test pass, so it should be approved.

summary.problem: django/core/paginator.py Paginator class lacked an __iter__ method, so iterating pages required manually looping over page_range and calling page().
summary.solution: The patch adds an __iter__ method to Paginator that yields self.page(page_num) for each page_num in self.page_range, plus a corresponding test. This is exactly the requested feature and matches the root-cause location (the point of creation, the Paginator class itself).
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly and minimally implements the requested feature at the right location; all 21 pagination tests pass and manual verification confirms correct page objects/order.

summary.problem: In Axes.hist() (lib/matplotlib/axes/_axes.py), when density=True the line `hist_kwargs = dict(density=density)` replaced the whole hist_kwargs dict, discarding the previously set 'range' key, so np.histogram ignored the user-supplied range.
summary.solution: The patch changes `hist_kwargs = dict(density=density)` to `hist_kwargs['density'] = density`, preserving the existing 'range' entry. This fixes the root cause at the point where hist_kwargs is assembled, exactly matching my proposed fix. It also adds a regression test test_hist_density_range asserting bins span (0,1).
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly fixes the root cause; direct verification shows bins now span the specified range with density=True while density normalization and density=False behavior remain correct.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/ticker.py, LogLocator.nonsingular and LogitLocator.nonsingular unconditionally reorder limits via `if vmin > vmax: vmin, vmax = vmax, vmin`, which destroys the reversed ordering that set_xlim/set_ylim rely on to invert a log/logit axis.
summary.solution: The patch adds a `swapped` flag in both LogLocator.nonsingular and LogitLocator.nonsingular; after performing the positivity/singularity normalization it re-swaps vmin/vmax so the original (possibly inverted) ordering is preserved. This targets the exact point where the wrong value was created (the locator's nonsingular), matching the identified root cause and mirroring the order-preserving behavior of MaxNLocator.nonsingular used for linear scales.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause in the correct file/functions and covers both affected log paths (LogLocator and LogitLocator); reproduction and regression tests pass, so it should be approved.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/legend.py, Legend.__init__ uses `isinstance(parent, Figure)` which excludes SubFigure (a FigureBase subclass, not a Figure), raising TypeError when calling SubFigure.legend().
summary.solution: The patch changes the local import from `Figure` to `FigureBase` and the type check from `isinstance(parent, Figure)` to `isinstance(parent, FigureBase)`. This exactly matches the root cause: SubFigure and Figure both derive from FigureBase, so accepting FigureBase allows subfigure legends while still accepting regular figures.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the exact location identified by the issue reporter; reproduction works, and Figure/Axes legends plus the full test_legend.py suite (88 passed) still pass.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/colorbar.py, Colorbar._add_solids unconditionally sliced divider segments with np.dstack([X, Y])[1:-1], dropping the first and last edges; when extend is used these extremity boundaries (between the extend triangles/rectangles and the inner solids) were never drawn even with drawedges=True.
summary.solution: The patch replaces the unconditional [1:-1] slice with logic that depends on self._extend_lower()/self._extend_upper(): keeps all edges for extend='both', keeps one end for 'min'/'max', and preserves [1:-1] for 'neither'. This is exactly at the root-cause location and function, matching the reviewer's independent proposal.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; verified segment counts (neither=8, both=10, min/max=9) confirm extremity edges are now drawn, and all 56 existing colorbar tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/dates.py ConciseDateFormatter.format_ticks, the check `if level < 2: show_offset = False` also disabled the offset at level 1 (months), so when plotting <1 year without January the year appeared nowhere (offset was empty).
summary.solution: The patch modifies exactly that code block: it only disables the offset when level==0, and at level==1 disables the offset only if January (month value 1) is among the ticks (in which case the year already appears in a tick via zero_formats[1]='%Y'); otherwise the offset (with '%Y') is kept, showing the year. This matches the identified root cause location and depth precisely.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause (the show_offset gating logic) rather than a symptom, correctly restores the year offset when January is absent, and preserves the no-redundant-year behavior when January is present.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/__init__.py RcParams.__getitem__, resolving rcParams['backend'] when it holds the _auto_backend_sentinel unconditionally calls plt.switch_backend(sentinel), which runs close('all') and destroys all figures. After an rc_context, the sentinel is restored, so the first get_backend() re-resolves it and wipes Gcf.figs.
summary.solution: The patch modifies RcParams.__getitem__ so that when the sentinel is encountered and a backend module is already loaded (plt._backend_mod is not None), it resolves the value directly to the already-selected backend name (matplotlib.backends.backend) instead of calling switch_backend. This avoids the redundant backend switch and its close('all'). It only falls back to switch_backend when no backend has been loaded yet (in which case no figures exist). This is the point where the erroneous re-resolution originates, i.e. the root cause.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch prevents the unnecessary re-resolution of the auto backend sentinel at its source; bug reproduction, close(fig), and get_backend() correctness are verified, and no regressions are introduced (the 3 failing tests fail identically on the unpatched baseline).

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/patches.py Patch.draw(), a cbook._setattr_cm context manager deliberately overrode self._dash_pattern to (0, ...), forcing the dash offset to 0 ('Patch has traditionally ignored the dashoffset'), so the offset in ls=(offset,(on,off)) had no visual effect.
summary.solution: The patch removes the _setattr_cm block so draw() no longer zeroes the dash offset; the real self._dash_pattern (with correct offset from set_linestyle/_scale_dashes) is passed to gc.set_dashes() at line 552. This is exactly the root-cause location and matches the proposed fix. It also adds a regression test test_patch_dash_offset.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point where the offset was being discarded; rendering now differs by offset and all existing patch/axes tests pass.

summary.problem: In backend_bases.py FigureCanvasBase.__init__, `figure._original_dpi = figure.dpi` unconditionally reset _original_dpi; on unpickle a new canvas is created and this overwrote the unscaled _original_dpi with the already-HiDPI-scaled dpi, so re-applying device_pixel_ratio doubled dpi every roundtrip.
summary.solution: The patch guards the assignment with `if not hasattr(figure, '_original_dpi')`, so the pickled _original_dpi (the true unscaled value) is preserved when the canvas is recreated during __setstate__. This fixes the point where the wrong reference value was created, matching the identified root cause. A regression test in test_pickle.py verifies dpi stays stable across repeated pickling.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; the doubling bug is reproduced without it and eliminated with it, and all pickle/figure tests pass.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/stackplot.py, stackplot() called axes.set_prop_cycle(color=colors), which both rejected CN color aliases (via validate_color_for_prop_cycle) and mutated the Axes property cycle.
summary.solution: The patch removes the set_prop_cycle call and instead builds a local color iterator: when colors is provided it uses itertools.cycle(colors) with mcolors.to_rgba to resolve CN references, otherwise it falls back to axes._get_lines.get_next_color. Fill_between calls now use this local get_next_color. This matches the identified root cause exactly and fixes both the CN alias error and the cycler mutation.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; CN colors work, the Axes cycler is no longer altered, default cycling still works, and existing tests pass.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/cbook/__init__.py, _safe_first_finite() uses `next(val for val in obj if safe_isfinite(val))`, which raises StopIteration when all values are non-finite (e.g. all-NaN x data), breaking ax.bar via _convert_dx.
summary.solution: The patch wraps the generator `next(...)` in a try/except StopIteration and falls back to `next(iter(obj))`, returning the first element when no finite element exists. This is exactly the root-cause location and function, and mirrors the semantics of safe_first_element, so it fixes all callers rather than just _convert_dx.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the point of creation; bug reproduction now returns a one-Rectangle BarContainer with nan x/height and regression tests pass.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/axes/_base.py __clear() (and figure.py Figure.clear/delaxes), children/artists were deparented via `self._children = []` etc. without unsetting each artist's `.axes` and `.figure` attributes, unlike Artist.remove().
summary.solution: The patch iterates over children in __clear() (and over artists/lines/patches/texts/images/legends in Figure.clear, plus delaxes) setting their `.axes` and `.figure` to None before clearing the lists. This modifies the exact root-cause locations where deparenting occurs, matching Artist.remove() behavior for both cla()/clear() and clf()/figure.clear().
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location for all relevant code paths; the reported case and additional scenarios verify correctly and the full axes/figure/legend test suites pass.

defects.description: The patch introduces trailing whitespace on several blank lines and uses redundant hasattr(self, 'child_axes')/hasattr(self, 'legend_') guards (these attributes are always present at this point). Purely cosmetic; no behavior impact.
defects.suggestion: Remove trailing whitespace and the unnecessary hasattr guards for cleanliness.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/colors.py Colormap.__call__, when input X has a small integer dtype (e.g. uint8), xa keeps that dtype; only the float branch did xa.astype(int). Assigning _i_over (N+1=257), _i_under (N=256), _i_bad (N+2=258) into a uint8 array triggers NumPy 1.24 out-of-bound integer deprecation warnings.
summary.solution: The patch moves `xa = xa.astype(int)` out of the `if xa.dtype.kind == 'f'` block so it always runs, wrapped in np.errstate(invalid='ignore') to preserve NaN-to-int handling. This ensures xa is always a wide int type before the over/under/bad index assignments. It matches the identified root cause: same file, function, and location, fixing the dtype at creation rather than guarding at point of use.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause (small integer dtype of xa) at the correct location and eliminates the warnings while preserving correct output for uint8, float, NaN, masked, and over/under-range inputs.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/offsetbox.py, DraggableBase.__init__ stored self.canvas = self.ref_artist.figure.canvas, a non-picklable backend canvas (e.g. FigureCanvasQTAgg), so pickling a figure with a draggable legend/annotation raised TypeError: cannot pickle 'FigureCanvasQTAgg'.
summary.solution: The patch removes the stored self.canvas attribute and replaces it with a canvas property deriving from self.ref_artist.figure.canvas, so the non-picklable object is never held in instance state. It also adds __getstate__ (dropping transient non-picklable attributes _c1 and background) and __setstate__ (reconnecting the pick/release callbacks via the ref_artist's canvas on unpickle). This targets the exact root-cause location: the point where the canvas reference is created/stored.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the true root cause at the creation point rather than guarding at the point of use, correctly handles both draggable legends and annotations, and preserves post-unpickle draggable behavior by reconnecting callbacks.

summary.problem: cbook.Grouper._mapping stores weakref.ref objects that cannot be pickled; after Figure.align_labels() populates Figure._align_label_groups Groupers, pickle.dumps(fig) raises TypeError: cannot pickle 'weakref.ReferenceType' object.
summary.solution: The patch adds __getstate__/__setstate__ to cbook.Grouper: __getstate__ dereferences the weakrefs into a list of strong-object groups, and __setstate__ rebuilds the weakref-based _mapping via join(). This is precisely at the root-cause location (where weakrefs are created/stored), matching the proposed fix, rather than a downstream guard in Figure.__getstate__.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; the reported case now pickles/unpickles successfully with alignment relationships preserved, and all relevant cbook/pickle tests pass.

defects.description: The added test_grouper_pickle contains trailing whitespace (flagged during git apply) and mixes a Figure-based fixture into a cbook unit test; functionally correct but slightly noisy style-wise.
defects.suggestion: Trim trailing whitespace; the Grouper pickle round-trip could be tested with lightweight weak-referenceable objects instead of a full Figure.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/cm.py ColormapRegistry.register, the registered copy retained the original cmap.name (e.g. 'some_cmap_name') while being stored under a different registry key (e.g. 'my_cmap_name'); set_cmap then wrote cmap.name into rcParams['image.cmap'], and subsequent get_cmap lookups failed with 'Colormap some_cmap_name is not recognized'.
summary.solution: The patch modifies ColormapRegistry.register to set cmap_copy.name = name on the stored copy so a registered colormap's .name always matches its registry key. This is exactly the root-cause location (point of creation/registration), not a symptom guard at the point of use. Copy semantics are preserved so the caller's original colormap is unaffected. It also updates/adds tests accordingly.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; reproduction of the reported scenario now succeeds, rcParams and imshow use the correct registered name, and the full test_colors.py suite plus related image tests pass.

summary.problem: Feature request: Text objects always read rcParams['text.antialiased'] at draw time (in backends' draw_text/draw_mathtext) and lack per-artist get/set_antialiased like other Artists.
summary.solution: The patch adds _antialiased state plus get_antialiased/set_antialiased (and an 'antialiased'/'aa' alias and constructor kwarg) to Text, defaulting to rcParams. In Text.draw() it propagates the value via gc.set_antialiased(). The agg and cairo backends now read gc.get_antialiased() instead of rcParams, and the value is threaded through MathTextParser.parse -> _parse_cached -> Output.to_raster for mathtext. This matches the identified root cause: creation of the antialias flag at the artist level and its consumption via the GraphicsContext at draw time.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct, complete implementation at the right locations; feature verified to change actual rendering and all relevant test suites pass.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/figure.py, SubFigure._redo_transform_rel_fig() computes each subfigure's bbox purely from width/height ratios, ignoring the gridspec's wspace/hspace, so those parameters have no effect.
summary.solution: The patch modifies the correct location (_redo_transform_rel_fig) by, for the non-constrained-layout path, calling self._subplotspec.get_position(self.figure), which does account for wspace/hspace. It also replaces the subfigure's shared subplotpars with SubplotParams(left=0,right=1,bottom=0,top=1,...) intending to neutralize figure margins. wspace/hspace now do change the gap between subfigures, but the margin-neutralization is ineffective: get_position resolves to the parent/root figure's subplotpars (default left=0.125/right=0.9/bottom=0.11/top=0.88), so subfigures are now inset by these margins.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: while the patch does make wspace/hspace take effect, it introduces a correctness regression where default subfigures no longer tile the full [0,1] figure area (now inset to [0.125,0.11]-[0.9,0.88]), breaking 4 existing image-comparison tests.

defects.description: For the default case (no wspace/hspace), subfigures previously spanned the full figure [0,0]-[1,1]. After the patch they only span [0.125,0.11]-[0.9,0.88] because get_position(self.figure) applies the root figure's subplot margins (left/right/bottom/top). The intended neutralization via setting self.subplotpars to left=0,right=1,... is ineffective because self.figure does not resolve to this SubFigure's subplotpars. This breaks default subfigure layout and fails existing tests: test_subfigure, test_subfigure_ss, test_subfigure_double, test_subfigure_scatter_size.
defects.suggestion: Do not route through get_position, which applies figure margins. Instead keep the ratio-based x0/y0/dx/dy computation and add only wspace/hspace spacing (as fractions of average cell size) without any left/right/bottom/top margins.

defects.description: Applying the patch causes 4 existing subfigure image-comparison tests to fail (RMS differences), confirming the default-layout regression is user-visible.
defects.suggestion: Fix the layout computation so default subfigures continue to tile the full figure area while wspace/hspace add spacing.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/axes/_axes.py hexbin(), when C is not None the mincnt condition used `len(acc) > mincnt` (with None mapped to 0), inconsistent with the C-is-None branch which uses `>=` (accum < mincnt), so mincnt=1 required >=2 points.
summary.solution: The patch changes `len(acc) > mincnt` to `len(acc) >= mincnt` at the correct root-cause location, which fixes the explicit mincnt=N case. However it leaves the `if mincnt is None: mincnt = 0` default unchanged. Combined with `>= 0` this now includes EVERY cell (even empty ones) in the default (no-mincnt, C-supplied) case, whereas previously only cells with >=1 datum were shown.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the patch introduces a correctness regression in the default C-supplied case (shows empty cells and calls reduce_C_function on empty arrays, e.g. np.mean emits 'Mean of empty slice' and produces NaN), which the patch's own tests do not cover. The None default should be 1, not 0.

defects.description: With C supplied and no mincnt (mincnt is None), the code sets mincnt = 0 and then evaluates len(acc) >= mincnt, i.e. >= 0, which is always true. This now renders ALL grid cells including empty ones, and calls reduce_C_function on empty lists. Pre-patch this default showed 51 cells (>=1 datum); post-patch it shows all 113 cells. With reduce_C_function=np.mean this emits 'Mean of empty slice' RuntimeWarnings and produces NaN. This is a behavior regression for the default case that the issue explicitly wanted preserved.
defects.suggestion: In hexbin(), change the default from `if mincnt is None: mincnt = 0` to `if mincnt is None: mincnt = 1` so combined with len(acc) >= mincnt the default correctly shows only cells with at least one datum, matching the C-is-None branch.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/category.py StrCategoryConverter.default_units (together with axis.py Axis.set_units), plotting categorical data on a twinx axis creates a fresh UnitData and propagates it to all shared axes, overwriting ax1's existing category mapping and firing units callbacks that call ax1.relim(), which drops the stackplot PolyCollection datalim, leaving ax1.dataLim.intervaly = [inf, -inf].
summary.solution: The patch fixes the propagation at its source: (1) default_units reuses an existing UnitData from a shared axis instead of creating a new one, and (2) set_units only fires the units callback for axes whose units object actually changes (identity check). This prevents ax1.relim() from being spuriously triggered when ax2 acquires the shared categorical units. This is upstream of relim in the root-cause chain; relim not supporting collections is a documented intentional limitation, so the true defect is the destructive unit propagation, which this patch targets.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly and minimally fixes the reported bug at its source; ax1.dataLim is preserved and the shared category mapping is made consistent, with all relevant test suites passing.

summary.problem: In lib/mpl_toolkits/axes_grid1/inset_locator.py, AnchoredLocatorBase.__call__ passes renderer=None (from _tight_bbox.adjust_bbox) to get_window_extent, which then dereferences self.figure._get_renderer() while self.figure is None, raising AttributeError.
summary.solution: The patch sets self.figure = ax.figure and, when renderer is None, resolves a renderer via self.figure._get_renderer() before calling get_window_extent. This fixes the point of creation (the locator __call__) rather than guarding at the crash site, matching the identified root cause. It also adds a regression test using fig.savefig(bbox_inches='tight').
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; reproduction succeeds without error and existing inset/anchored-locator tests still pass.

summary.problem: In lib/matplotlib/text.py, _AnnotationBase.__init__ stored the xy argument by reference (self.xy = xy), so mutating the array passed to annotate() later moved the annotation/arrow.
summary.solution: The patch changes 'self.xy = xy' to 'self.xy = tuple(xy)' in _AnnotationBase.__init__, converting the input into an immutable tuple copy so subsequent mutations of the caller's array no longer affect the annotation. This is exactly the root-cause location (point of creation), not a downstream guard. xytext is already unpacked into scalars (x, y = xytext) so it needed no change.
summary.overall_assessment: The fix addresses the true root cause with a minimal, correct change; the reproduction case is fixed and all text/offsetbox tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In seaborn/_core/scales.py ContinuousBase._setup, legend labels are built via axis.major.formatter.format_ticks(locs), which for large-magnitude data drops the ScalarFormatter multiplicative offset, producing wrong labels (e.g. '1','2' instead of '1e6','2e6').
summary.solution: The patch keeps format_ticks but, when the formatter reports a non-empty get_offset(), rebuilds labels using formatter.format_data(loc) per tick, which yields full-value representations including the offset. This is at the exact root-cause location (legend label creation) and matches the proposed fix location.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: large-number legends now show correct values (verified '1e6'..'5e6'), small-number legends unchanged, and all existing scale/legend tests pass.

defects.description: The included test hunk contains trailing whitespace that corrupts the diff so the test portion does not apply cleanly with git apply; only the source hunk applies. The core source fix is unaffected and existing tests pass.
defects.suggestion: Strip trailing whitespace from the added test block so the full patch applies cleanly.

summary.problem: In requests/models.py PreparedRequest.prepare_method(), 'self.method.upper()' preserves unicode for a unicode input (e.g. u'POST'), which infects headers and causes a UnicodeDecodeError during body concatenation in Python 2.
summary.solution: The patch wraps the result in to_native_string(): self.method = to_native_string(self.method.upper()). This converts the method to a native str (bytes on Py2) at the point of creation, so the method no longer propagates unicode into headers. to_native_string is already imported in models.py, and None input is still handled by the surrounding guard.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the exact root cause identified (prepare_method) at the point of creation; verified under Python 2.7 that u'POST' becomes native str 'POST' and relevant existing tests pass.

summary.problem: In requests/auth.py build_digest_header(), the qop-options directive was emitted unquoted ('qop=auth'), violating RFC2617 which requires it to be a quoted string.
summary.solution: The patch changes the format string on the qop line from ', qop=auth, ...' to ', qop="auth", ...', quoting the qop value. This is exactly at the root cause location (the point where the header string is created) and matches the fix I independently proposed.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly fixes the root cause; the generated header now contains qop="auth" and all existing digest auth tests pass.

summary.problem: In requests/sessions.py merge_setting(), None-valued headers were only removed if present in request_setting, so setting a session default header (e.g. session.headers['Accept-Encoding']=None) left the None value in the merged result and it was sent as the literal string 'None'.
summary.solution: The patch fixes both affected code paths: (1) the 'request_setting is None' branch now returns a copy of session_setting with None-valued keys filtered out, and (2) the merge path now computes none_keys from merged_setting instead of only request_setting. This directly addresses the root cause (removal only considered request_setting) rather than a symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch changes the exact root-cause function (merge_setting) and covers both the reported scenario (session-default None) and the request-level None case; verification tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In requests/models.py PreparedRequest.prepare_url, ASCII hostnames with an empty leading label (e.g. '.example.com') were not validated, so instead of raising InvalidURL they leaked a low-level UnicodeError from the idna codec.
summary.solution: The patch changes the ASCII-host guard from `elif host.startswith(u'*')` to `elif host.startswith((u'*', u'.'))`, so hosts beginning with an empty label (leading dot) now raise InvalidURL('URL has an invalid label.'). This is exactly the root-cause location in prepare_url and matches my proposed fix. It also adds 'http://.example.com' to the test_preparing_bad_url parametrization.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly fixes the root cause at the point of URL validation and produces the expected InvalidURL exception; verified with reproduction and regression tests.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/variable.py, as_compatible_data() unconditionally ran `data = getattr(data, 'values', data)`, so any object with a .values attribute (e.g. HasValues) had its .values extracted and coerced during Variable.__setitem__ assignment into object arrays.
summary.solution: The patch guards the `.values` extraction so it only occurs when the object is array-like (has ndim, shape, and dtype attributes), which is exactly the root-cause location (line 221 in as_compatible_data). This preserves pandas/xarray coercion while leaving arbitrary objects untouched. It also adds a regression test.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the point of value creation, not a symptom patch; reproduction is fixed and no regressions were introduced.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/variable.py IndexVariable.copy, the deep-copy path built PandasIndexAdapter(self._data.array.copy(deep=True)) without passing the original dtype, so unicode <U* dtypes (stored in pandas Index as object) were re-inferred as object.
summary.solution: The patch passes dtype=self._data.dtype into the PandasIndexAdapter constructor in the deep-copy branch, preserving the stored dtype. This is exactly the root-cause location (point of creation), matching my proposed fix, and adds a regression test test_copy_index_unicode_dtype.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct minimal fix at the root cause; bug reproduction, deep/shallow copy, copy.copy/deepcopy, MultiIndex and numeric-coord regressions all pass.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/combine.py, combine_by_coords ran the monotonicity check over all concatenated.dims (line 504), incorrectly requiring identical 'bystander' coordinate dimensions (which are excluded from concat_dims in _infer_concat_order_from_coords) to be monotonic, raising ValueError.
summary.solution: The patch changes `for dim in concatenated.dims:` to `for dim in concat_dims:` so the monotonicity check only applies to dimensions actually concatenated. This is exactly the root cause: bystander dims are already correctly skipped as concat candidates but were still being checked. It also adds a regression test and a whats-new entry.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location with no side effects; reproduction works, all 67 combine tests pass including the existing non-monotonic-concat-dim error test.

summary.problem: Variable.quantile (xarray/core/variable.py) returned Variable(new_dims, qs) dropping attrs and had no keep_attrs param, and Dataset.quantile (dataset.py) never passed keep_attrs down to var.quantile, so DataArray/variable-level attrs were lost even with keep_attrs=True.
summary.solution: The patch adds a keep_attrs parameter to Variable.quantile, resolves it via _get_keep_attrs, and attaches self._attrs to the result when True; and Dataset.quantile now passes keep_attrs to var.quantile (moving the _get_keep_attrs default resolution before the loop). This targets exactly the root cause at both the Variable creation site and the Dataset propagation site.
summary.overall_assessment: Approve: the patch fixes the point where attrs were dropped (Variable.quantile) and correctly propagates keep_attrs from Dataset; all repro, edge-case, and regression tests pass.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/merge.py, dataset_merge_method() passes `other` directly to merge_core without converting a DataArray to a Dataset (unlike the top-level merge()), so coerce_pandas_values calls `.items()` on the DataArray and raises AttributeError.
summary.solution: The patch adds a local `from .dataarray import DataArray` import and, at the start of dataset_merge_method, does `other = other.to_dataset()` when `other` is a DataArray. This is exactly the root-cause location and mirrors the coercion already done in the top-level merge(). It also updates type hints and the docstring for Dataset.merge.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of creation and passes reproduction, regression, and full test suite; approve.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/dataarray.py, DataArray.integrate used a 'dim' parameter, inconsistent with Dataset.integrate and differentiate which use 'coord'.
summary.solution: The patch renames the primary argument to 'coord' while keeping 'dim' as a deprecated alias that emits a FutureWarning, raises ValueError if both are given, and raises ValueError if neither is given. It updates the docstring and adds a Deprecations entry to whats-new.rst. This fixes the root cause (the parameter definition itself) rather than a symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch addresses the exact root cause with a proper deprecation cycle and maintains backward compatibility; all existing integrate tests pass and new behaviors verified.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/weighted.py, boolean weights caused dot() in _sum_of_weights to return a boolean (True) instead of the numeric count, yielding wrong weighted mean (2.0 instead of 1.0).
summary.solution: The patch adds a conversion in Weighted.__init__ that casts boolean weights to float (weights.astype(float)) before storing them. This is the point of creation, so both _weighted_sum and _sum_of_weights receive numeric weights, fixing all affected code paths rather than a single symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct (deepest) location and all 967 weighted tests pass, including new boolean-weight tests for mean/sum/sum_of_weights.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/dataarray.py DataArray.to_unstacked_dataset, `self.sel({variable_dim: k}).squeeze(drop=True)` leaves a leftover scalar coordinate named after the stacked dim (e.g. 'y') on each selected variable; for single-dim variables squeeze cannot drop it (it is a scalar coord, not a size-1 dimension), so merging into a Dataset raises MergeError due to conflicting 'y' values.
summary.solution: The patch appends `.drop_vars(dim, errors='ignore')` after the squeeze, removing the leftover stacked-dim coordinate from each variable before building the Dataset. This is at the exact root-cause location (same file/function/line) and fixes the point where the conflicting coordinate is created, matching the proposed fix. A regression test for GH4094 is added.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; single-dim and multi-dim roundtrips both produce identical Datasets and all existing stacked_array tests pass.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/nanops.py, _maybe_null_out() explicitly raised ValueError for tuple/list axis and used mask.shape[axis] which cannot index by a tuple, so sum/prod with min_count over multiple dims errored.
summary.solution: The patch removes the ValueError guard for multi-dimension reductions and replaces mask.shape[axis] with np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod(), which correctly computes the total element count across one or multiple reduced axes. This is exactly the root-cause location (matches my independent proposal) and depth in the call stack.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause; the reported ValueError is gone and multi-dim min_count reductions produce correct results with all 596 duck_array_ops tests passing.

defects.description: For a full reduction to a scalar (result.ndim == 0), min_count is still ignored due to a pre-existing bug in the elif branch where getattr(result,'dtype') in dtypes.NAT_TYPES erroneously evaluates True for float dtypes. This is a pre-existing issue (present in unpatched code for 1-D-to-scalar reductions), NOT introduced by this patch, and is outside the scope of the reported issue which is only about the raised error.
defects.suggestion: Out of scope for this fix; could be addressed separately by using np.issubdtype/explicit dtype comparison instead of the 'in NAT_TYPES' membership check.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/computation.py, polyval evaluated the polynomial on the DataArray's datetime64 data (converted with a fixed 1970-01-01 offset in _ensure_numeric) instead of on the (timedelta) coordinate index used by the old 2022.3.0 behavior, producing values ~1e30 instead of the correct results.
summary.solution: The patch makes polyval use the dimension coordinate (coord.coords[dim]) when a 1-D DataArray has a matching index, restoring coordinate-based evaluation, and changes _ensure_numeric to pass offset=None for timedelta64 (kind 'm') while keeping 1970-01-01 for datetime64. This matches the reported example and fixes that case, but the offset=None choice for timedelta is incorrect.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the reported example but introduces a high-severity correctness regression: offset=None makes datetime_to_numeric subtract the minimum timedelta, so any timedelta coordinate not starting at zero yields shifted (wrong) results.

defects.description: For timedelta64 arrays (dtype.kind == 'm') the patch passes offset=None to datetime_to_numeric. With offset=None, datetime_to_numeric sets offset to the array minimum and subtracts it, shifting the data. For a timedelta coordinate that does not start at zero (e.g. [10s,20s,30s]) polyval p(t)=t returns [0,1e10,2e10] instead of the correct [1e10,2e10,3e10]. The reported example only works because its timedelta coordinate starts at 0; the patch's own added 'timedelta' test also starts at 0, so it passes by coincidence and does not detect the bug.
defects.suggestion: In _ensure_numeric.to_floatable(), use a zero timedelta offset for timedelta64 instead of None, e.g. offset = np.datetime64('1970-01-01') if x.dtype.kind == 'M' else np.timedelta64(0, 'ns'), so no minimum-based shift is applied.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/common.py get_chunksizes(), the guard `hasattr(v.data, "chunks")` accesses `v.data`, which forces a lazily-loaded (non-dask) zarr array to be fully read into memory when accessing Dataset.chunks.
summary.solution: The patch fixes the root cause in common.py by removing the `v.data` access and iterating `v.chunksizes.items()` directly, and changes Variable.chunksizes to use `self._data.chunks` instead of `self.data.chunks` (both good). However, it also ADDS a new branch to Variable.chunksizes that, when the array is not dask but has `encoding['preferred_chunks']`, returns `self.encoding['preferred_chunks']` directly, which changes documented behavior and returns the wrong data format.
summary.overall_assessment: The memory-loading root cause is correctly fixed, but the extra preferred_chunks branch introduces a high-severity correctness defect (wrong output format and inconsistent/undocumented behavior), so changes are required.

defects.description: The added `elif "preferred_chunks" in self.encoding` branch returns `self.encoding['preferred_chunks']`, which for zarr is a mapping of {dim: int} (a single chunk length per dim, see backends/zarr.py line 449). But chunksizes/Dataset.chunks is contracted to return Mapping[Hashable, tuple[int, ...]] (a tuple of block lengths per dim). Verified with a real zarr dataset chunked (4,4) over a 10x10 array: a dask-opened dataset yields chunks={'x': (4,4,2), 'y': (4,4,2)}, but the patched lazy open yields chunks={'x': 4, 'y': 4} - bare ints, not block-length tuples, and different values than the equivalent chunked dataset. Additionally, Variable.chunks (line 988, unchanged) still returns None for the same variable, so Variable.chunks and Variable.chunksizes now disagree in content, contradicting the docstring that says they differ only in format. This also changes the documented semantics ('None if the underlying data is not a dask array').
defects.suggestion: Remove the `elif "preferred_chunks" in self.encoding` branch from Variable.chunksizes. The common.py change alone fixes the reported bug (avoids loading data); for non-dask lazy zarr, Dataset.chunks should return an empty Frozen({}) as before. If exposing preferred chunks is desired, it must be converted into proper tuple-of-block-lengths and applied consistently to both Variable.chunks and Variable.chunksizes, which is a separate feature.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/rolling.py, DataArrayRolling.__iter__ computed only right-aligned window start/stop indices and ignored self.center, so manual iteration produced non-centered windows unlike .mean().
summary.solution: The patch modifies __iter__ (the exact root-cause function) to compute centered start/stop offsets (offset = w // 2) when self.center[0] is True, and pads out-of-bounds windows with NaN via maybe_promote + pad so counts/min_periods handling yields the same NaN edges as the reduction. Labels remain at their original positions. This matches my proposed fix at the correct call-stack depth.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause (center ignored in __iter__) and iteration now matches .mean() for both odd and even windows; full rolling test suite (1796 passed) and reproduction confirm correctness.

summary.problem: In xarray/core/dataset.py Dataset.reset_index, when drop=True the dropped variable name is removed from `variables` but not from `coord_names`, leaving a stale coord_name (e.g. 'z') with no backing variable, so DataVariables.__len__ (len(_variables) - len(_coord_names)) goes negative and raises ValueError.
summary.solution: The patch changes `coord_names = set(new_variables) | self._coord_names` to `(set(new_variables) | self._coord_names) - set(drop_variables)` in reset_index, purging the dropped variable names from coord_names. This is exactly the root-cause location (point of creation of the inconsistent state), not a symptom guard in DataVariables.__len__. It also adds a regression test.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause where the inconsistent state is created, restoring the invariant coord_names is a subset of variables; reproduction is fixed and the full test_dataset.py suite passes (371 passed).

summary.problem: In xarray/core/rolling.py Coarsen.construct, line 976 computed should_be_coords as `set(window_dim) & set(self.obj.coords)`, which only re-declares coordinates whose name matches a coarsened dimension, so non-dimensional coordinates (e.g. `day`) get demoted to data variables.
summary.solution: The patch replaces line 976 with `should_be_coords = set(obj.coords.keys())`, restoring the full set of original coordinates after reshaping. This is exactly the root-cause location and function I identified. It also adds a regression test in test_coarsen.py.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point where the coordinate set is (incorrectly) narrowed, and all coordinates - dimensional and non-dimensional - are preserved for both Dataset and DataArray inputs.

summary.problem: In pylint/pyreverse/inspector.py, attribute types were derived only by inferring the assigned value (handle_assignattr_type); PEP 484 type annotations were never consulted, so `self.a = a` with `a: str = None` produced no useful type (inference of the None default gave only NoneType).
summary.solution: The patch adds annotation-based type extraction at the point where instance_attrs_type is populated: (1) handle_assignattr_type now inspects the enclosing function's argument annotations when the assigned value is a parameter name, and (2) a new _handle_annassign_type handles class-body AnnAssign nodes (e.g. dataclass fields). This matches the identified root cause and depth (point of creation, not point of use), covering both the __init__-parameter path and the class-body annotation path.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly addresses the root cause by feeding annotation types into instance_attrs_type; reproduction now shows the type hint (e.g. `a : NoneType, str`, `b : int`) and all existing pyreverse tests pass.

defects.description: For `a: str = None` the rendered attribute is `a : NoneType, str` rather than just `str`, because the inferred None default is retained alongside the annotation type. The requested type is shown, so it is functionally correct but slightly noisier than the ideal output.
defects.suggestion: Optionally prefer/prioritize the annotation type over an inferred NoneType default when a default of None is present, to render `a : str`.

summary.problem: In pylint/checkers/variables.py, _store_type_annotation_node() only handled astroid.Name and astroid.Subscript nodes; an Attribute node like 'abc.ABC' in a type comment fell through the early 'return' without recording 'abc', causing a false unused-import.
summary.solution: The patch restructures _store_type_annotation_node so the Subscript-specific typing handling is nested, and any other annotation (including Attribute nodes) falls through to extract all astroid.Name nodes via nodes_of_class, so 'abc' from 'abc.ABC' is now recorded. It also adds a dotted-prefix startswith check when matching imports against type-annotation names. This addresses the exact root-cause location and logic.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; reproduction case no longer emits unused-import, genuinely unused imports are still flagged, and all existing/new tests pass.

summary.problem: In pylint/config/__init__.py the PYLINT_HOME default was hardcoded to '.pylint.d'/'$HOME/.pylint.d', not XDG-compliant.
summary.solution: The patch refactors PYLINT_HOME computation into _get_pylint_home(), which honors PYLINTHOME first, then XDG_DATA_HOME/pylint, then defaults to ~/.local/share/pylint, with '.pylint.d' only as a fallback when no home dir exists. It also switches os.mkdir to os.makedirs (needed for the nested XDG path) and updates docs/help text. This directly changes the root-cause location.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the exact location identified; all 53 tests in tests/lint/unittest_lint.py pass and end-to-end save/load works with the new XDG path.

summary.problem: pylint/lint/pylinter.py `_discover_files` walks directories via os.walk and yields every .py file / package root without applying --ignore, --ignore-patterns, or --ignore-paths, so ignored dirs like `.a` are never pruned in recursive mode.
summary.solution: The patch converts `_discover_files` to an instance method and prunes matching directories in-place during os.walk via a new `_is_ignored_directory` helper checking config.ignore (basename), config.ignore_patterns (basename), and config.ignore_paths (full path). This is the correct root-cause location, but the ignore_paths check matches an anchored regex against the un-normalized path `os.path.join(root, d)` (e.g. './.a'), which fails, so --ignore-paths does not work.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the fix is at the right location but only partially works - --ignore and --ignore-patterns are fixed while --ignore-paths (explicitly required by the problem statement) still fails to ignore the directory.

defects.description: `_is_ignored_directory` matches config.ignore_paths regex against `os.path.join(root, d)`, which for a top-level run (`pylint --recursive=y .`) produces paths like './.a'. Since ignore-paths patterns are compiled and matched with re.match() (anchored at start), a pattern such as '.a' or '^\.a' never matches './.a'. Reproduction confirmed: `--ignore-paths=.a` and `--ignore-paths="^\.a"` still analyze .a/foo.py, exactly the failing command from the problem statement. Thus one of the three ignore settings the issue requires is not fixed.
defects.suggestion: Normalize the directory path before matching (e.g. os.path.normpath) and/or match ignore_paths against a path form consistent with how expand_modules matches, so anchored patterns match. Ensure the fix covers --ignore, --ignore-patterns, AND --ignore-paths.

defects.description: The added tests (test_recursive_ignore_paths_dir etc.) assert only code=0. Running the same directory WITHOUT any ignore also yields code=0 (subdirectory/module.py produces no lint errors), so these tests pass trivially and do not actually verify that ignoring occurred - hiding the --ignore-paths defect above.
defects.suggestion: Use a target that produces lint errors when NOT ignored, and assert that the ignored module does not appear in output (or that exit code differs), so the test meaningfully verifies the ignore behavior.

summary.problem: In pylint/lint/run.py, _query_cpu() computes avail_cpu = int(cpu_shares / 1024) (or int(cpu_quota/cpu_period)), which returns 0 for Kubernetes values (e.g. shares=2), and _cpu_count() propagates that 0 via min(cpu_share, cpu_count), causing multiprocessing.Pool to raise 'Number of processes must be at least 1'.
summary.solution: The patch correctly fixes the production root cause: it adds `or 1` to both avail_cpu computations in _query_cpu and changes _cpu_count to `return max(1, min(cpu_share, cpu_count))`, ensuring the value is never 0. However, the patch also adds tests/lint/test_run.py whose tests fail: they patch `pylint.lint.run.Path` via side_effect but the code opens the cgroup files with literal string paths through builtin open(), which is not mocked, causing FileNotFoundError.
summary.overall_assessment: The source fix is at the correct root-cause location and is logically sound, but the patch introduces three failing tests, so it must be changed before approval.

defects.description: The added tests (test_query_cpu_with_kubernetes_values, test_query_cpu_with_fractional_cpu, test_cpu_count_never_zero) fail with FileNotFoundError. They mock pylint.lint.run.Path to redirect .is_file() checks, but _query_cpu() opens the cgroup files via builtin open() using literal absolute string paths, which the mock does not intercept, so open() hits the non-existent real path.
defects.suggestion: Also patch builtins.open (or the file reads) so the mocked temp files are actually opened, e.g. mock both pylint.lint.run.Path and open to return the temp file contents; or restructure the test to mock the file reads consistently.

summary.problem: In pylint/lint/pylinter.py `_discover_files`, individual .py files yielded from os.walk (the non-package else branch) were not filtered through `_is_ignored_file`, so files matching `ignore-paths` (e.g. ^src/gen/.*$) were still checked under --recursive=y.
summary.solution: The patch replaces the plain generator yielding all .py files with a loop that calls `_is_ignored_file(filepath, self.config.ignore, self.config.ignore_patterns, self.config.ignore_paths)` and only yields files that are not ignored. This is at the exact root-cause location (point of file creation/discovery) I identified independently in Step 3, and applies ignore-paths to individual files.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; reproduction confirms ignored files are now skipped while others remain, and the full unittest_lint suite (56 tests, including the added regression test) passes.

summary.problem: In pylint/__init__.py, modify_sys_path() unconditionally executes sys.path.pop(0), removing the first entry even when it is not the cwd/''/'.', breaking runpy.run_module(alter_sys=True) usage that prepends real paths.
summary.solution: The patch guards the pop with `cwd = os.getcwd(); if sys.path[0] in ('', '.', cwd): sys.path.pop(0)`, only removing the first entry when it represents the working directory. This is precisely the root-cause location and matches the canonical upstream fix, and the docstring is updated accordingly.
summary.overall_assessment: Approve: the patch fixes the exact broken logic at the point of creation, reproduces-and-fixes the reported scenario, and all related tests pass.

summary.problem: In pylint/config/argument.py, _regexp_csv_transfomer (and its sibling _regexp_paths_csv_transfomer) split option values naively on every comma via _csv_transformer/_splitstrip, so regexes containing commas (e.g. {1,3}) are mangled and re.compile crashes.
summary.solution: The patch replaces the naive comma split with a quote-aware csv.reader in both _regexp_csv_transfomer and _regexp_paths_csv_transfomer, and updates _parse_rich_type_value in config/utils.py to quote list items containing commas so TOML list values round-trip correctly. This changes exactly the root-cause location I identified and fixes both sibling code paths.
summary.overall_assessment: The fix is at the correct root-cause location, addresses both regexp-csv transformers, and provides the comma-escaping mechanism the reporter explicitly said would be acceptable; the idiomatic TOML list form now works and all config tests pass.

defects.description: The exact minimal config from the report (bare TOML string bad-names-rgxs = "(foo{1,3})", which yields the unquoted string (foo{1,3})) still crashes with the same re.error, because csv.reader only preserves commas inside quoted fields. Users must instead use a TOML list or an inner-quoted string. This matches the intended design (comma is the delimiter) and the reporter accepted an escape mechanism, but the literal reported snippet is not fixed.
defects.suggestion: Document (and/or in the changelog) that comma-containing regexes must be provided as a TOML list or quoted.

defects.description: _parse_rich_type_value quotes comma-containing list items but escapes embedded double quotes with a backslash instead of the CSV-standard doubling. Since csv.reader uses doublequote=True with no escapechar by default, a pattern containing BOTH a double quote and a comma is mis-parsed into broken fragments. Rare edge case for name regexes; does not regress prior already-broken behavior.
defects.suggestion: Escape embedded quotes by doubling them or use csv.writer to serialize the list.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/unittest.py TestCaseFunction.runtest, the guard `not _is_skipped(self.obj)` only checks the test method for `__unittest_skip__`, so class-level @unittest.skip is missed and tearDown() is postponed/run under --pdb.
summary.solution: The patch changes the line 319 condition to `... and not _is_skipped(self._testcase) and not _is_skipped(self.obj)`, checking the test instance (which reads the class-level `__unittest_skip__` attribute) as well as the method. This is exactly the root cause location and depth I identified, and it also handles pytest.mark.skip at class level. A parametrized regression test was added.
