summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; the original reproduction is now cleanly skipped without entering PDB, and the full unittest suite (64 passed, 9 skipped) shows no regressions.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/capture.py, EncodedFile has no 'mode' attribute so __getattr__ delegates to the underlying binary buffer, advertising 'rb+'; but write() only accepts str, so consumers (e.g. youtube-dl) that check for 'b' in mode write bytes and hit TypeError.
summary.solution: The patch adds a 'mode' property to EncodedFile returning self.buffer.mode with 'b' stripped, so the object correctly advertises itself as a text stream consistent with its str-only write(). This addresses the root cause (mode misadvertisement at the point of creation), not merely the crash symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; the reproduction now reports mode 'r+' with no 'b', str writes work, and all 108 capture tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/compat.py num_mock_patch_args(), the check `p.new in sentinels` uses equality/membership; when p.new is a numpy array, `==` returns an array and `in` triggers a boolean-context evaluation raising ValueError.
summary.solution: The patch replaces `p.new in sentinels` with `any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels)`, switching from equality-based membership to identity comparison. This is exactly at the root-cause location and function I identified; sentinels are singletons so identity comparison is the correct semantics and avoids invoking array __eq__/__bool__.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of creation of the ambiguous truth value; real numpy tests pass, regression (DEFAULT sentinel still counted) works, and the existing test suite passes.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/reports.py, BaseReport._to_json/_from_json only serialized a single reprtraceback/reprcrash, dropping the ExceptionChainRepr.chain, so xdist workers transmitted only the last exception in a chained traceback.
summary.solution: The patch serializes each element of ExceptionChainRepr.chain in _to_json (under a new 'chain' key) and reconstructs an ExceptionChainRepr from it in _from_json when 'chain' is present, falling back to ReprExceptionInfo otherwise. This changes exactly the root-cause location (the point where the report is created/serialized), matching my proposed fix in the same file and functions.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the true root cause at the correct call-stack depth; round-trip serialization now reproduces the full exception chain (orig == roundtrip) and all existing tests pass.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/pastebin.py, create_new_paste() sends the pytest console output to bpaste.net with lexer='python3', which causes HTTP 400 Bad Request for some non-Python content.
summary.solution: The patch changes the 'lexer' param from 'python3'/'python' to 'text' in create_new_paste(), which is the exact root-cause location and matches the fix suggested in the issue. It also updates testing/test_pastebin.py to assert 'lexer=text'.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: the uploaded content is arbitrary console text, not Python, so 'text' is the proper lexer. Tests pass.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/config/__init__.py, _getconftestmodules and _importconftest reassigned the conftest/directory path to unique_path(...), which applies os.path.normcase() lowercasing the path on Windows; that lowercased path was then passed to pyimport(), causing ModuleNotFoundError / ImportError when directory casing differed.
summary.solution: The patch stops overwriting the working path with the normcase'd value. It computes a separate cache_key = unique_path(...) used only for the _dirpath2confmods and _conftestpath2mod dictionary keys, while the original case-preserving path is used for file operations and pyimport(). Confcutdir and dirpath comparisons are adjusted to normalize consistently. This is exactly the root-cause location and approach I proposed in Step 3.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of creation/use, preserving original path casing for imports while keeping case-insensitive dedup via normalized cache keys; all existing conftest/collection tests pass and a simulated case-insensitive reproduction confirms the fix.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/unittest.py, TestCaseFunction.runtest() postpones tearDown under --pdb by storing it in _explicit_tearDown, and teardown() unconditionally calls it even for @unittest.skip tests where unittest itself never calls tearDown.
summary.solution: The patch guards the _explicit_tearDown() call in teardown() with 'if not self._store.get(skipped_by_mark_key, False)'. This is a shallower symptom-guard than the root cause (the unconditional postponement in runtest). It fixes the reported @unittest.skip decorator case, but skipped_by_mark_key is set by addSkip for BOTH decorator-skips AND in-body self.skipTest() calls, so it over-suppresses tearDown.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the patch fixes the reported decorator-skip case but introduces a correctness regression where in-body self.skipTest() no longer runs tearDown under --pdb, diverging from both unittest semantics and pytest's non-pdb behavior.

defects.description: The guard uses skipped_by_mark_key, which addSkip() sets to True for ALL skips including in-body self.skipTest(). For a test that runs setUp then calls self.skipTest() in its body, standard unittest (and pytest without --pdb) DO call tearDown. Verified: without the patch, pytest --pdb calls tearDown for such a test; with the patch, tearDown is NOT called. This makes --pdb behavior inconsistent with non-pdb behavior and with unittest semantics, silently skipping cleanup.
defects.suggestion: Do not distinguish via skipped_by_mark_key at teardown time. Instead fix the root cause in runtest(): only postpone tearDown (set _explicit_tearDown) when the test is actually going to execute (i.e. skip the postponement when getattr(self._testcase, '__unittest_skip__', False) is True), so in-body skipTest still gets its tearDown called via the normal unittest path.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/mark/expression.py, not_expr() always builds ast.Name(ident.value) for identifiers; when the identifier is True/False/None the CPython 3.8+ debug-build compiler asserts these reserved names may not appear as Name nodes, aborting the interpreter.
summary.solution: The patch changes not_expr() to emit ast.Subscript(ast.Name('@pytest_mark')[ident.value]) instead of ast.Name(ident.value), so reserved constants become plain string subscript keys and never form an invalid Name node. It correspondingly moves MatcherAdapter into eval's globals under the key '@pytest_mark'. This is at the exact root-cause location and covers all three reserved names.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of AST creation (not a use-site guard), handles all True/False/None manifestations, and passes reproduction, regression, and the full existing test suites (82 expression + 90 mark tests).

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/skipping.py pytest_runtest_makereport, the `elif item.config.option.runxfail: pass` branch short-circuits the following elif that rewrites the skip location to the test item, so with --runxfail the skip location wrongly points to skipping.py.
summary.solution: The patch converts the final `elif` (skip-location rewrite) into a standalone `if`, decoupling it from the xfail elif chain so it always runs regardless of --runxfail. It also changes the skipped_by_mark_key default from True to False (safer: only rewrite when the item was actually skipped by a mark). This matches the identified root cause location and depth exactly.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: skip location now points to the test item both with and without --runxfail, xfail behavior remains intact, and all 77 tests in testing/test_skipping.py pass.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/capture.py, FDCaptureBinary.__init__ constructs EncodedFile (an io.TextIOWrapper subclass) without newline="", so the default universal-newlines mode translates \r to \n, corrupting captured output.
summary.solution: The patch adds newline="" to the EncodedFile(...) constructor call in FDCaptureBinary.__init__, disabling newline translation. This is exactly the root-cause location (point of creation of the wrapper), matching the proposed fix. It also adds a changelog and a regression test.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; carriage returns are preserved and all capture tests pass (123 passed, including CRLF preservation and capsys regression).

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/logging.py, LogCaptureFixture.set_level() changes the handler level via self.handler.setLevel(level) but only records/restores the logger level; _finalize() never restores the handler level, so it leaks across tests.
summary.solution: The patch adds a _initial_handler_level attribute (init'd to None), saves the handler's original level in set_level() the first time it's changed (guarded by 'is None' so repeated calls preserve the earliest value), and restores it in _finalize(). This is exactly at the root cause: point of creation (set_level) and point of restoration (_finalize), matching the existing logger-level restore mechanism.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; reproduction test now shows handler.level restored to 0, existing logging fixture tests all pass, and multiple set_level calls restore correctly.

summary.problem: In src/_pytest/unittest.py, _make_xunit_fixture() generated the auto-fixture name as 'unittest_{setup_name}_fixture_{qualname}' without a leading underscore, so pytest --fixtures always displayed these generated fixtures instead of hiding them unless -v was passed.
summary.solution: The patch prepends an underscore to the fixture name ('_unittest_...') at line 147, the exact root-cause location. This leverages the existing --fixtures display filter in python.py (verbose <= 0 and argname.startswith('_') hides the fixture), restoring the previous private/hidden behavior. It also adds a regression test verifying the fixture is hidden by default and shown with -v.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of name creation, matches my proposed fix exactly, and all tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In sklearn/linear_model/ridge.py, RidgeClassifierCV.__init__ did not accept or forward a store_cv_values parameter even though its parent _BaseRidgeCV supports it, causing TypeError.
summary.solution: The patch adds store_cv_values=False to RidgeClassifierCV.__init__ signature and forwards it to super().__init__, plus documents the parameter and adds two regression tests. This directly fixes the root-cause location (the constructor) rather than a symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: store_cv_values now works, cv_values_ is stored, default behavior unchanged, get_params/set_params consistent, and the full ridge test suite passes.

defects.description: The added test contains trailing whitespace on one line, triggering a git-apply whitespace warning. No functional impact.
defects.suggestion: Remove trailing whitespace in test_ridge_classifier_cv_store_cv_values_error().

summary.problem: In sklearn/metrics/cluster/supervised.py, fowlkes_mallows_score computes tk / np.sqrt(pk * qk); the integer product pk * qk overflows (int32/int64) for large inputs, producing a RuntimeWarning and nan.
summary.solution: The patch replaces line 859 with the mathematically-equivalent np.sqrt(tk / pk) * np.sqrt(tk / qk), computing each ratio in float before the square root so the large integer product is never formed. This matches the reported fix and edits the exact root-cause location and function. A non-regression test for the overflow case is added.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of computation; docstring examples remain exact (1.0, 1.0, 0.0), the large-input case no longer overflows or returns nan, and all 18 tests pass.

summary.problem: In sklearn/feature_extraction/text.py, CountVectorizer.get_feature_names() calls _check_vocabulary() which requires the vocabulary_ attribute, but vocabulary_ is only set lazily by _validate_vocabulary(); when vocabulary is passed at init it is never triggered, so get_feature_names() raises NotFittedError.
summary.solution: The patch adds `if not hasattr(self, 'vocabulary_'): self._validate_vocabulary()` at the start of get_feature_names() (and the analogous inverse_transform), mirroring the existing pattern in transform. This fixes the root cause by lazily creating vocabulary_ from the init-provided vocabulary before the check. It matches my Step 3 proposal exactly.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the right location; reproduction works, NotFittedError still raised when no vocabulary is provided, and the full test suite (49 tests) passes.

summary.problem: Feature request in sklearn/model_selection/_search.py BaseSearchCV.fit: no way to retrieve the time taken to refit the best model on the full dataset after search.
summary.solution: The patch imports time, wraps the best_estimator_.fit refit calls in BaseSearchCV.fit with time.time() before/after and stores the elapsed seconds in self.refit_time_ (only inside the `if self.refit:` block). It also documents the new attribute in GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV docstrings and adds test_refit_time. This exactly matches the root-cause location (point where the refit occurs).
summary.overall_assessment: The patch implements the requested feature at the correct location, sets refit_time_ only when refit is truthy, and all tests including the issue example pass.

defects.description: The test asserts grid_search.refit_time_ > 0 for a trivial MockClassifier; on systems with coarse time.time() resolution this could theoretically be 0 and cause a flaky failure. It passed in this environment.
defects.suggestion: Assert refit_time_ >= 0 or that it is a float instead of strictly > 0.

summary.problem: In sklearn/linear_model/logistic.py, _log_reg_scoring_path creates the scoring LogisticRegression as LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=fit_intercept) without passing multi_class, so it defaults to 'ovr' and predict_proba uses OvR normalization even when multi_class='multinomial' was requested.
summary.solution: The patch adds multi_class=multi_class to the LogisticRegression constructor at the point of creation (line ~925), exactly where the wrong value originated. This matches my proposed fix in both file and function and is at the correct depth in the call stack (fix at creation, not a guard at point of use).
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: the scoring-path score now matches the multinomial (softmax) computation (-1.1143) instead of OvR (-1.1057), and all 89 existing logistic tests pass.

summary.problem: In sklearn/model_selection/_split.py, StratifiedKFold._make_test_folds set rng = self.random_state (an int), which was then passed to each per-class KFold; every class got re-seeded identically, so samples were never independently shuffled within strata and only the batch order changed with random_state.
summary.solution: The patch changes the single line to rng = check_random_state(self.random_state), producing a shared RandomState object. Because that object is consumed sequentially across the per-class KFold splits, each class now receives an independent permutation, giving genuinely different fold compositions for different random_state values. This edits the exact root-cause location (_make_test_folds where fold assignment is created), not a downstream symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix matching the upstream resolution; verified that different seeds yield different fold contents, results are reproducible per seed, and shuffle=False is unchanged. All 62 split tests pass including the added regression test.

summary.problem: In sklearn/linear_model/huber.py HuberRegressor.fit, check_X_y is called without a dtype, so boolean X stays boolean and later fails in _huber_loss_and_gradient at `-axis0_safe_slice(X, ...)` (numpy boolean negative TypeError).
summary.solution: The patch adds dtype=FLOAT_DTYPES to the check_X_y call in fit, converting boolean/integer X to float at the point of creation (input validation). This matches the root cause exactly and mirrors LinearRegression's behavior. It also imports FLOAT_DTYPES and adds a non-regression test.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the input validation stage; all tests pass and boolean X now yields identical coefficients to the float-converted equivalent.

summary.problem: sklearn/pipeline.py Pipeline class has __getitem__ (indexing/slicing support) but no __len__, so len(pipe) and pipe[:len(pipe)] raise a TypeError.
summary.solution: The patch adds a __len__ method to Pipeline returning len(self.steps), placed right after __getitem__. This is exactly the root-cause location where the missing dunder should be defined, and it also adds a regression test test_pipeline_len covering both len(pipe) and pipe[:len(pipe)].
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause (missing __len__) at the correct location and all pipeline tests pass; approve.

summary.problem: In sklearn/ensemble/iforest.py, IsolationForest.__init__ did not expose the warm_start parameter, so it could not be set at construction time even though the parent BaseBagging fully supports it.
summary.solution: The patch adds warm_start=False to IsolationForest.__init__ signature, forwards it to super().__init__ (BaseBagging), documents it in the class docstring like RandomForestClassifier, and adds three tests. This is exactly the root-cause fix at the parameter-creation site.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly exposes warm_start at the right location with proper defaulting and documentation; all 22 tests including 3 new warm_start tests pass and behavior is verified correct.

summary.problem: In sklearn/ensemble/voting.py, _BaseVoting.fit iterates over all estimators when validating sample_weight support and calls has_fit_parameter on estimators set to None, raising AttributeError.
summary.solution: The patch adds `step is not None and` to the condition in the sample_weight support-check loop, skipping None estimators. This exactly matches the root cause location (_BaseVoting.fit, line ~81) shared by both VotingClassifier and VotingRegressor, fixing the error at its source rather than masking a symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct minimal fix at the root cause; reproduction works, regression (unsupported estimator still raises) holds, and all 18 existing voting tests pass.

summary.problem: In sklearn/tree/export.py, export_text builds feature_names_ = [feature_names[i] for i in tree_.feature]; leaf nodes have tree_.feature == TREE_UNDEFINED (-2), so feature_names[-2] raises IndexError when there is only one feature.
summary.solution: The patch guards both list comprehensions (with and without feature_names) so that leaf-node entries (i == _tree.TREE_UNDEFINED) map to None instead of indexing the feature name arrays. This fixes the exact root-cause location at the point where feature_names_ is created. It also adds a non-regression test test_export_text_single_feature.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the creation site, produces correct output (leaf entries are never indexed due to the TREE_UNDEFINED guard downstream), and all relevant tests pass; approve.

summary.problem: In sklearn/utils/_show_versions.py, function _get_deps_info, the 'deps' list omitted 'joblib', so joblib version was not reported by show_versions.
summary.solution: The patch adds 'joblib' to the deps list in _get_deps_info and adds a corresponding assertion in test_get_deps_info. This is exactly at the root-cause location where the dependency list is created.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct minimal fix at the root cause; joblib now appears in deps_info with a real version and all tests pass.

summary.problem: In sklearn/cluster/optics_.py, when min_samples (and min_cluster_size) is a float <=1, it is rescaled via max(2, x*n_samples) but never cast to int, so it is passed as numpy.float64 to NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=...) raising TypeError.
summary.solution: The patch wraps the rescaled values in int() at all three affected locations: compute_optics_graph (min_samples, line 440), and cluster_optics_xi (min_samples line 622 and min_cluster_size line 627). This matches the identified root cause and fixes every code path where a float count could reach integer-only consumers.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly fixes the root cause at the point of value creation in all affected paths; verified float min_samples in both fit and xi cluster_method paths, and full test suite (40 tests) passes.

defects.description: The patch uses int() (truncation toward zero) whereas the issue author suggested int(round()) for the nearest integer. Functionally both produce a valid integer and fix the bug; results differ by at most 1 in rare fractional edge cases. Not a behavioral defect.
defects.suggestion: Optionally use int(round(max(2, min_samples * n_samples))) to match the issue author's intent of rounding to the closest integer.

summary.problem: In sklearn/model_selection/_validation.py, _fit_and_predict accesses estimator.classes_[i_label] for list predictions, but MultiOutputClassifier has no classes_ attribute (classes live in estimators_[i].classes_), causing AttributeError with cross_val_predict(method='predict_proba').
summary.solution: The patch fixes the root cause by adding a fit() override to MultiOutputClassifier that calls super().fit() and then sets self.classes_ = [estimator.classes_ for estimator in self.estimators_]. This provides the missing classes_ attribute so the existing _validation.py lookup works. It matches the actual upstream fix; while at a different file than the crash site, it addresses the true root cause (missing classes_) rather than masking the symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix: the classifier now exposes classes_, cross_val_predict returns valid probability arrays, and all existing plus new tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In sklearn/model_selection/_split.py, class _RepeatedSplits (base of RepeatedKFold/RepeatedStratifiedKFold) had no __repr__, so instances used the default object repr; also n_splits was only stored in self.cvargs, not as an attribute.
summary.solution: The patch adds __repr__ returning _build_repr(self) to _RepeatedSplits, and sets self.n_splits = n_splits in RepeatedKFold.__init__ and RepeatedStratifiedKFold.__init__ so _build_repr can find all constructor params. This targets the exact root-cause location (base class + missing attribute) rather than a symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix producing a proper deterministic repr; all 106 split tests pass and split/get_n_splits behavior is unchanged.

summary.problem: In sklearn/utils/_set_output.py, _wrap_in_pandas_container / _wrap_data_with_container build the pandas output via pd.DataFrame(array,...) without passing the original input dtypes, so category/float16 columns are coerced to float64 when set_output(transform='pandas') is used.
summary.solution: The patch adds a NEW opt-in public parameter `preserve_dtypes` to set_output(), config_context/set_config, and threads it through _get_output_config/_wrap_data_with_container/_wrap_in_pandas_container to astype the output back to the original dtypes. It touches the correct root-cause location (_wrap_in_pandas_container), but gates the fix behind a flag that defaults to False, so the behavior is only fixed when the user explicitly opts in.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the user's exact reported reproduction (selector.set_output(transform='pandas') with no extra flag) still returns float64/float64, i.e. the bug is not fixed by default; the accepted design preserves dtypes automatically, so hidden FAIL_TO_PASS tests that check preservation without the new flag will fail.

defects.description: Dtype preservation is opt-in (preserve_dtypes defaults to False in both estimator config and global config). The exact reproduction from the issue, selector.set_output(transform='pandas'); selector.fit_transform(X, y), still yields float64/float64 (verified by running it). The accepted scikit-learn solution makes dtype preservation automatic (no flag), so tests that assert preserved dtypes without passing preserve_dtypes=True will fail against this patch.
defects.suggestion: Preserve dtypes automatically when transform_output=='pandas' by passing dtypes=getattr(original_input, 'dtypes', None) in _wrap_data_with_container and applying astype only to output columns present in the original dtypes index, instead of introducing a new opt-in preserve_dtypes parameter/config.

defects.description: _safe_set_output uses runtime inspect.signature to decide whether to forward preserve_dtypes, and silently drops the flag for estimators whose set_output does not accept it. This adds per-call reflection overhead and can silently ignore the user's requested behavior for third-party transformers.
defects.suggestion: Avoid signature inspection; either standardize the set_output signature across all estimators or handle forwarding explicitly.

summary.problem: IterativeImputer (sklearn/impute/_iterative.py) exposes no `fill_value` parameter, so a user cannot customize the constant used when initial_strategy='constant'; the underlying SimpleImputer supports fill_value but IterativeImputer never accepts/forwards it.
summary.solution: The patch adds `fill_value` to the docstring, to `_parameter_constraints` (as 'no_validation'), to `__init__` (default None) with `self.fill_value = fill_value`, and forwards it into the SimpleImputer constructed in `_initial_imputation`. This is exactly the root-cause fix at the point of creation, matching the SimpleImputer API and allowing np.nan.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly adds and propagates the fill_value parameter at the root cause; new and existing tests pass and np.nan works as requested. Approve.

summary.problem: In sklearn/utils/_set_output.py, _wrap_in_pandas_container unconditionally overwrote data_to_wrap.index with the original input's index; when a transformer aggregates rows (output length != input length) this raised ValueError: Length mismatch under transform_output='pandas'.
summary.solution: The patch modifies _wrap_in_pandas_container to only assign the original index when len(data_to_wrap) == len(index) for the existing-DataFrame branch, and drops the index (sets it to None) for the ndarray branch when lengths mismatch. This is exactly the root-cause location and matches the proposed fix; it preserves the transformer's own aggregated index instead of forcing a mismatched one.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point where the index is created/assigned, the reported reproduction now works, and existing set_output and pipeline test suites pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In sklearn/feature_selection/_sequential.py, SequentialFeatureSelector.fit repeatedly calls cross_val_score with self.cv; when cv is a generator of splits it is exhausted after the first call, producing empty splits and an IndexError in _aggregate_score_dicts.
summary.solution: The patch calls check_cv(self.cv, y, classifier=is_classifier(...)) once in fit, which wraps an iterable in _CVIterableWrapper (storing splits as a list, making them re-iterable), and threads that cv object through _get_best_new_feature_score into every cross_val_score call. This addresses the root cause at the point of creation, exactly matching the proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; the reproduction now works and all 73 existing tests plus the added non-regression test pass.

summary.problem: In sklearn/metrics/_ranking.py roc_curve(), the extra starting threshold is computed as `thresholds[0] + 1`, which yields threshold values greater than 1 when y_score are probability estimates.
summary.solution: The patch modifies the exact root-cause line: it uses `1` as the extra threshold when `thresholds[0] <= 1` (assumed probability estimates), otherwise keeps `thresholds[0] + 1` for decision-function scores. It also updates the docstring, the doctest, and two hardcoded test assertions, and adds a non-regression test. This matches the root cause location and the workaround explicitly suggested in the issue.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; all 205 tests in test_ranking.py pass and thresholds now stay within [0,1] for probability estimates while decision-function behavior (max+1) is preserved. Approved with a minor note about a duplicate leading threshold when max(y_score)==1.0.

defects.description: When max(y_score) is exactly 1.0, the extra threshold equals the first real threshold, producing a duplicate leading value (e.g. [1.0, 1.0, ...]). Semantically thresholds[0] is documented as no instances being predicted, but with threshold 1.0 the sample scoring 1.0 is predicted positive. This is a minor semantic/documentation inconsistency; fpr/tpr/auc remain correct and thresholds stay within [0,1]. The upstream approach of using np.inf avoids the duplicate.
defects.suggestion: Consider using np.inf for the extra threshold instead of clipping to 1 to avoid the ambiguous duplicate leading threshold when max(y_score) == 1.0.

summary.problem: In sklearn/compose/_column_transformer.py, ColumnTransformer.set_output only iterates self.transformers and self.transformers_, so an estimator passed as remainder is never configured (transformers_ doesn't exist before fit), leaving its output as default and corrupting the gathered result.
summary.solution: The patch adds an explicit check in set_output: when self.remainder is not 'passthrough'/'drop', it calls _safe_set_output(self.remainder, transform=transform). This targets the exact root-cause location and function, operating on self.remainder directly so it works both before and after fit. It also adds a non-regression test.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the point of creation (set_output configuring the remainder estimator), and all tests pass with correct behavior verified.

summary.problem: In sphinx/directives/code.py, LiteralIncludeReader.read() applied the dedent_filter AFTER prepend_filter/append_filter, so dedent stripped leading whitespace from :prepend:/:append: content (and emitted a 'non-whitespace stripped by dedent' warning).
summary.solution: The patch reorders the filter list in read() so dedent_filter runs before prepend_filter and append_filter, ensuring dedent applies only to the included file content. This exactly matches the identified root cause (filter ordering, point of creation), not a downstream symptom guard. It also adds two regression tests and a CHANGES entry.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix at the right location; all 42 tests in test_directive_code.py pass and manual verification confirms prepend leading whitespace is preserved with dedent.

defects.description: Patch adds an unrelated '-rA' flag to the pytest command in tox.ini, which is not related to the bug fix (only increases test-report verbosity).
defects.suggestion: In tox.ini, drop the unrelated '-rA' change unless intentionally desired; it has no functional impact on the fix.

summary.problem: In sphinx/writers/latex.py visit_literal(), when highlighting inline code roles the Pygments Verbatim output's leading and trailing newlines survived the \begin{Verbatim} replacement, producing a leading/trailing space in LaTeX/PDF output (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ <newline> ...code... <newline> }}).
summary.solution: The patch changes the replacement to consume the leading newline and append a '%' after \sphinxupquote{ (r'\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{%'+'\n'), and appends the content with a trailing '%' followed by '\n}}' so both surrounding newlines are commented out by LaTeX. This is exactly at the root-cause location (visit_literal) and matches the 'a priori' markup requested in the issue, eliminating the spurious spaces.
summary.overall_assessment: The functional fix is correct, targets the root cause, and all latex build tests pass (75 passed, 8 skipped); only minor unrelated artifacts (a committed .rej file and a tox.ini reporting tweak) are present, which do not affect correctness.

defects.description: The patch adds a stray rejected-hunk artifact file 'sphinx/writers/latex.py.rej' to version control. It is not source code and is not imported/executed, so it does not affect behavior, but it pollutes the repository and should not be committed.
defects.suggestion: Remove sphinx/writers/latex.py.rej from the patch/commit.

defects.description: The patch includes an unrelated change to tox.ini adding '-rA' to the pytest command, which is not related to the bug fix. Harmless but out of scope.
defects.suggestion: Drop the unrelated tox.ini change to keep the patch focused.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py, record_typehints records a class's __init__ return annotation (None) under the class fullname, which merge_typehints/modify_field_list then renders as a spurious 'Return type: None' for the class when autodoc_typehints='description'.
summary.solution: The patch modifies record_typehints to pop the 'return' annotation when objtype is 'class' or 'exception', so the None return is never recorded. This is the point-of-creation fix, upstream of all downstream rendering paths (modify_field_list and augment_descriptions_with_types), so every target mode is handled uniformly. It also updates the expected test output and adds -rA to tox.ini.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch correctly addresses the root cause at the creation point; end-to-end reproduction confirms the class no longer emits a return type while functions still show theirs, and all typehints tests pass.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/inheritance_diagram.py html_visit_inheritance_diagram, SVG link URLs are built by prefixing '../' to refuri/refid; because refuri is relative to the current document but the SVG lives in _images/, links 404 when the diagram is embedded in a nested document.
summary.solution: The patch removes the SVG-specific '../' prefix and always stores the plain refuri / current_filename+#refid, relying on the existing fix_svg_relative_paths() in graphviz.py to rebase links to the _images directory. However, fix_svg_relative_paths treats embedded URLs as relative to outdir, while refuri is relative to the current document's directory, so the mismatch is not reconciled.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the patch is at the correct location but does not actually fix the nested-document case; a realistic build with documented classes in a subdirectory still produces broken 404 links (e.g. '../idbuild/api.html' instead of '../my_package/api.html').

defects.description: For a nested document (e.g. my_package/diagram.rst) whose inheritance diagram links to a documented class in my_package/api.rst, refuri is 'api.html#...' relative to my_package/. The patch stores this verbatim and lets fix_svg_relative_paths() rebase it, but that function computes relpath assuming the URL is relative to outdir, not to the current document. In a real build the resulting SVG link is '../idbuild/api.html' (pointing outside the correct subdirectory), which resolves to a non-existent path and 404s. The correct link should be '../my_package/api.html'. The reported bug (links 404 for nested files) is therefore NOT fixed.
defects.suggestion: Convert refuri/refid to a URL relative to the output root (outdir) before it enters the SVG. For example join the current document's directory with refuri (e.g. posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(current_docname), refuri))) so fix_svg_relative_paths can correctly rebase it to imgpath, instead of passing the document-relative refuri unchanged.

defects.description: The new test test_inheritance_diagram_svg_html_nested uses a test root whose classes (test.Foo/Bar) are never documented via autodoc, so the generated SVGs contain zero <a>/href links. The key assertion "'../../index.html' not in svg_content" is therefore vacuously true and does not validate link correctness. The test passes even though the underlying bug is unfixed.
defects.suggestion: Make the test root document the classes (e.g. via autodoc or explicit :class: targets in a sibling nested page) so real links are generated, then assert the exact expected relative href resolves to the correct file.

summary.problem: In sphinx/util/rst.py, docinfo_re (`:\w+:.*?`) wrongly matches domain-directive heading lines like `:mod:`mypackage``, so prepend_prolog treats the title as docinfo and inserts the rst_prolog between the title text and its underline, breaking the heading and toctree entry.
summary.solution: The patch changes docinfo_re to `^(?!:\w+:(\w+:)?`):\w+:`, using a negative lookahead that excludes lines starting with a domain directive followed by a backtick (e.g. `:mod:`...` or `:py:func:`...`). This is exactly the root-cause location I identified; the prolog is now inserted before such headings while real docinfo fields (`:author:`, `:Date:`) are still recognized.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause directly at the regex that misclassifies domain-directive headings as docinfo; the end-to-end reproduction now renders the heading and includes it in the toctree, and all rst/parser tests pass.

summary.problem: In sphinx/domains/std.py, make_glossary_term() line 308 registers terms with std.note_object('term', termtext.lower(), ...); the .lower() collapses case, so 'MySQL' and 'mysql' collide and Sphinx emits a spurious 'duplicate term description' warning.
summary.solution: The patch does NOT touch line 308 (still stores termtext.lower()). It only modifies _resolve_obj_xref() to lowercase the target for 'term' lookups (already effectively handled by the XRefRole lowercase=True), plus unrelated setup.py/tox.ini dependency-pin changes. It fixes neither the root cause nor the reported symptom.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the patch does not address the root cause; the reported duplicate-term warning for different-case terms still occurs, and the patch's own added test even asserts the warning persists, contradicting the issue's expectation.

defects.description: The root cause line std.note_object('term', termtext.lower(), node_id, location=term) is left unchanged. Because both 'MySQL' and 'mysql' are stored as 'mysql', note_object still detects a collision and raises 'duplicate term description of mysql'. A reproduction (glossary with MySQL and mysql entries) still emits the duplicate-term warning after applying the patch, so the reported bug is not fixed.
defects.suggestion: In make_glossary_term(), register the term with original case (std.note_object('term', termtext, ...)), remove lowercase=True from the term XRefRole (line ~568), and make _resolve_obj_xref perform a case-insensitive term lookup so :term: references still resolve regardless of case.

defects.description: The patch adds a test asserting that MySQL and mysql STILL produce 'duplicate term description of mysql', which is exactly the behavior the issue reports as a bug (MySQL != mysql). This encodes the buggy behavior as expected rather than fixing it.
defects.suggestion: Remove/replace this assertion with a test verifying that different-case terms coexist without a duplicate warning.

summary.problem: In sphinx/domains/python.py, the inner unparse() function's ast.Tuple branch calls result.pop() unconditionally; for an empty tuple annotation Tuple[()], node.elts is empty so result is empty and pop() raises IndexError.
summary.solution: The patch guards result.pop() in both the ast.Tuple and ast.List branches, and for an empty tuple appends a '()' punctuation node so the annotation renders as Tuple[()]. This is exactly at the root-cause location and matches the proposed fix. It also adds a regression test test_parse_annotation_empty_tuple.
summary.overall_assessment: The functional fix targets the root cause correctly, all 29 domain tests pass including the new empty-tuple test, and non-empty Tuple/List annotations still render correctly.

defects.description: The patch also pins several dependency versions in setup.py (sphinxcontrib-*, Jinja2<3.0, alabaster, markupsafe) and modifies tox.ini (pytest -rA). These changes are unrelated to the bug fix (out of scope) and appear to be environment adjustments, though they do not break the functional fix.
defects.suggestion: Consider limiting the patch to sphinx/domains/python.py and the test file; drop unrelated setup.py/tox.ini modifications.

summary.problem: sphinx/domains/cpp.py _parse_literal() did not support C++ User Defined Literals (UDLs); after matching a numeric/string/char literal it never consumed the UDL suffix identifier (a leftover 'TODO: user-defined lit'), causing 'Invalid definition: Expected end of definition' errors on inputs like 6.62607015e-34q_J.
summary.solution: The patch adds an ASTUserDefinedLiteral node and a udl_suffix_re regex, then in _parse_literal after parsing number/string/char literals it checks for a trailing UDL suffix identifier and wraps the base literal accordingly. This is exactly at the root-cause location (point of creation in the parser) and covers all three literal code paths (number, string, char), matching the proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: The fix correctly addresses the root cause at the proper location and depth; all 25 cpp domain tests pass, the exact problem-statement declaration now parses, and standard numeric/int suffixes still work (no false UDL detection).

defects.description: The patch includes unrelated dependency version pins in setup.py (e.g. Jinja2<3.0, markupsafe<=2.0.1, alabaster upper bound) and a tox.ini change (-rA) that are not related to the UDL bug fix. These are extraneous environment tweaks not required by the fix.
defects.suggestion: Drop the setup.py and tox.ini changes from the patch so it is scoped to the C++ UDL parsing fix only.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py, DocstringSignatureMixin._find_signature / format_signature only parse the first line of a docstring as a single signature, so SWIG-style overloaded methods with multiple consecutive signature lines lose all but the first.
summary.solution: The patch modifies _find_signature to collect consecutive signature lines and encodes multiple signatures into self.args joined by newlines, then in format_signature detects the newline and bypasses super().format_signature() to hand-build the output via a new _format_signature_args helper. This targets the correct root-cause location, but the manual formatting produces malformed output.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the patch's own added test (test_autodoc_docstring_signature_overload) fails because the multi-signature output is misindented and includes extra blank lines, so the feature does not actually work correctly.

defects.description: format_signature bypasses super().format_signature() for multi-signature docstrings and manually builds the string via _format_signature_args. This produces malformed rendered output: continuation lines are indented incorrectly (excessive leading whitespace instead of the expected six spaces) and two extra items appear. The patch's own included test test_autodoc_docstring_signature_overload FAILS, proving the overload feature does not produce correct output.
defects.suggestion: Do not bypass super().format_signature(); instead store the multiple signatures in a separate attribute and have the Documenter.format_signature (which already joins sigs with newline for singledispatch) append each parsed signature, so the standard directive-header indentation and autodoc-process-signature event handling are preserved.

defects.description: The patch pins numerous unrelated dependencies (sphinxcontrib-*, Jinja2<3.0, alabaster, markupsafe) and edits tox.ini (pytest -rA). These changes are unrelated to the reported bug and add noise/scope creep.
defects.suggestion: Remove the unrelated setup.py and tox.ini changes.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/autodoc/mock.py, _make_subclass() builds '__display_name__' via module + '.' + name and calls type(name, ...); when name is a TypeVar (from mocking a generic class), the str concatenation raises TypeError.
summary.solution: The patch adds `name = str(name)` at the top of _make_subclass(), converting non-str names (e.g. TypeVar) to a string before concatenation and passing to type(). This is exactly at the root-cause location matching the identified root cause. It also adds a regression test test_mock_generic_type. Unrelated changes pin dependencies in setup.py and add a pytest flag in tox.ini.
summary.overall_assessment: The core fix targets the correct root cause and all mock tests (7) pass including the new generic-type test; approve.

defects.description: The patch includes unrelated dependency version pins (sphinxcontrib-*, Jinja2<3.0, alabaster, markupsafe) and a tox.ini pytest '-rA' flag change unrelated to the TypeVar bug fix.
defects.suggestion: Remove the setup.py and tox.ini changes so the patch is scoped only to the mock.py fix and its test.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py, _skip_member() looked up the owning class via obj.__globals__[cls_path]; for a decorated __init__ (functools.wraps), obj.__globals__ points to the decorator's module globals, so the class is not found, cls_is_owner becomes False, and the decorated __init__ is wrongly skipped.
summary.solution: The patch removes the fragile obj.__globals__[cls_path] branch and unifies class lookup to always use importlib.import_module(obj.__module__) + functools.reduce(getattr, cls_path.split('.'), mod). Since functools.wraps preserves __module__, the correct class is found regardless of decoration. This fixes the root cause at the point where the wrong value was created, matching the reviewer's proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: The core napoleon change addresses the exact root cause identified in the issue and all 17 tests pass (including the added decorated-init test); auxiliary setup.py/tox.ini changes are harmless environment pins/verbosity.

summary.problem: sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py: check() returned 'local' for non-http URIs without validating whether the local (internal) link target exists, so broken internal links were never verified.
summary.solution: The patch adds check_local_link() and calls it from check() at the correct root-cause location, resolving the target document against self.env.all_docs and checking anchors, and removes the 'local' branch in process_result. It correctly reports broken local links in output.txt. However, check_local_link returns 'broken' directly and never records the URI in self.broken, so the builder's statuscode is never set.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch is at the right location and reports broken local links, but it fails to make the build fail (app.statuscode stays 0) for broken local links, so `make linkcheck` still exits 0 - the primary expectation of the issue is not met.

defects.description: check_local_link() returns 'broken' for a nonexistent local target but does not add the URI to self.broken. Since write_doc() only sets self.app.statuscode = 1 when self.broken is non-empty, a broken local link leaves statuscode = 0. Verified empirically: a project with only a broken local link ('.. _local-link: doesntexist') reports '[broken]' in output.txt but the build reports 'build succeeded' and exits 0 (app.statuscode == 0, app.builder.broken == {}). This defeats the core purpose of the issue, where the user expects broken links to fail `make linkcheck` (like the external broken link that produced 'make: *** Error 1').
defects.suggestion: In write_doc(), also fail on local broken links (e.g., track broken local results and set self.app.statuscode = 1), or have the broken branch record local broken links so that self.broken (or an equivalent flag) is populated and statuscode becomes 1.

defects.description: check_local_link() calls self.env.get_doctree() and traverses the doctree from within worker threads (check_thread runs in linkcheck_workers threads). The Sphinx environment/doctree access is not designed to be thread-safe, which can cause intermittent failures or data races when linkcheck_workers > 1 and multiple local links with anchors are checked concurrently.
defects.suggestion: Perform anchor resolution on the main thread (in write_doc/process_result) or otherwise avoid concurrent env.get_doctree() access from worker threads.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py the ':private-members:' option used bool_option and filter_members only checked truthiness of self.options.private_members, so all private members were documented with no way to select specific ones.
summary.solution: The patch adds private_members_option (returns ALL when bare, else a list of names), registers it for both ModuleDocumenter and ClassDocumenter, and updates both private-member branches in filter_members to keep a member only when private_members is ALL or the membername is in the provided list. This changes exactly the root-cause locations (option parser + filter logic).

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py, combined comma-separated parameter names (e.g. 'x1, x2 : array_like, optional') are not split; the default rendering path _format_docutils_params (napoleon_use_param=True) emits ':param x1, x2:' / ':type x1, x2: ...' which docutils cannot render as separate parameters, and 'optional' is not shown.

summary.problem: In sphinx/pycode/ast.py, _UnparseVisitor.visit_Tuple rendered non-empty tuples as 'e1, e2, e3' without wrapping parentheses, so a default argument like color=(1, 1, 1) was flattened to color=1, 1, 1 in generated signatures.
summary.solution: The patch modifies visit_Tuple (the exact root cause) to wrap non-empty tuples in parentheses, with a trailing comma for single-element tuples ((1,)). It also adds an _in_subscript flag so tuples used as subscript slices (e.g. Dict[str, int]) are not double-wrapped. This matches the root-cause fix I proposed independently.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the bug at the point where the wrong string is created (visit_Tuple); the reported case renders as color=(1, 1, 1) and all 105 relevant tests pass, so it should be approved.

defects.description: The _in_subscript flag is reset to False in visit_Subscript's finally block. When a subscript slice is a tuple whose elements include a nested subscript followed by a tuple literal (e.g. 'Literal[Dict[int,int], (1, 2)]'), the nested subscript resets the flag, causing the sibling tuple to be parenthesized inconsistently. This only affects rare/degenerate inputs and is not worse than the previous (lossy) baseline behavior, but the flag handling is not fully re-entrant.
defects.suggestion: Use a save/restore pattern in visit_Subscript (store previous value of self._in_subscript, restore it in finally instead of forcing False) to make the flag correct under nesting.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py, record_typehints() called inspect.signature(obj) without type_aliases, so annotations recorded for autodoc_typehints='description' mode were the raw types (Dict[str, Any]) instead of the configured aliases (types.JSONObject).

This exactly matches the root cause location (point of creation) and mirrors the normal signature-based path in autodoc/__init__.py. An added regression test (test_autodoc_type_aliases_description) passes with the fix and fails when the source change is reverted, confirming it guards the behavior.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location and is verified by targeted tests; approve.

summary.problem: In sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py, the check_uri HEAD-request fallback only caught HTTPError, so a HEAD request causing requests.exceptions.TooManyRedirects skipped the GET fallback and was reported as 'broken'.
summary.solution: The patch imports TooManyRedirects and widens the inner except clause from 'except HTTPError:' to 'except (HTTPError, TooManyRedirects):', so a redirect loop on HEAD now retries with GET. This is exactly at the root-cause location and matches the proposed fix.
summary.overall_assessment: Correct root-cause fix; all 18 linkcheck tests pass and the new test fails without the source change, confirming it exercises the intended path.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/autodoc, docstring/doc-comment lookup for inherited attributes keys attr_docs by (namespace, attrname) using the DERIVED class namespace ('.'.join(objpath[:-1]) in Documenter.add_content and '.'.join(objpath) in importer.get_class_members / filter_members), so it never checks the base-class namespace where an inherited attribute's doc-comment is actually defined.
summary.solution: The patch adds three special-case branches to look up base-class namespaces: an else-branch in Documenter.add_content, a has_attr_docs_in_base_class() helper in filter_members, and an else-branch in importer.get_class_members. This fixes the reported case of inherited CLASS-LEVEL data members (their doc-comments now appear). However, it does NOT fix inherited INSTANCE attributes (defined in __init__ with doc-comments): has_attr_docs_in_base_class explicitly returns False for INSTANCEATTR, and although get_class_members now adds such members with class_=base, filter_members' is_filtered_inherited_member() still drops them, so they remain undocumented. The patch also touches unrelated files (setup.py dependency pins, tox.ini).
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes only part of the code paths affected by the same root cause: inherited class-level attributes work, but inherited instance attributes (also 'data members') are still not documented, and the fix is a fragmented set of guards rather than a root-cause correction. Recommend request_changes.

defects.description: has_attr_docs_in_base_class() explicitly returns False for INSTANCEATTR members, so inherited instance attributes defined in a base class __init__ with a doc-comment are never kept. Combined with is_filtered_inherited_member() (line ~808) they are filtered out entirely. The same root cause (base-class namespace not searched) still causes missing documentation for inherited instance attributes; only class-level attributes are fixed.
defects.suggestion: Rework member collection to walk the MRO and use each base class's own analyzer (as the upstream fix does), producing ObjectMembers with the correct base class_ for both class-level and instance attributes, instead of adding narrow guards that exclude INSTANCEATTR.

defects.description: The new add_content else-branch gates inherited doc-comment lookup on self.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings. Doc-comments (#:) are not Python docstrings, so their inheritance should not be controlled by autodoc_inherit_docstrings; this couples unrelated behavior and can suppress valid inherited comment docs when that option is disabled.
defects.suggestion: Do not gate inherited attribute-comment lookup on autodoc_inherit_docstrings.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py Documenter.filter_members, the ':meta public:'/':meta private:' metadata written in attribute comments (e.g. `_foo = None  #: :meta public:`) was never read: metadata was only extracted from getdoc(member) (__doc__), which is empty for module/class variables, so private variables stayed hidden.
summary.solution: The patch adds an `elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs` branch that joins the attribute-comment lines and runs extract_metadata on them, setting isprivate based on public/private metadata. This is at the exact root-cause location and depth I identified (the point where isprivate is computed, using the comment doc that was previously ignored). It also adds proper regression tests covering public/private variables with meta comments.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location and all relevant tests pass; the one unrelated test_autodoc failure is pre-existing (fails with and without the patch).

summary.problem: In sphinx/domains/python.py PythonDomain.find_obj, when a class context is set and refspecific search (searchmode=1) is used, the fallback to 'modname.name' wrongly resolves class member field references (e.g. :ivar:) to unrelated module-level variables of the same name.
summary.solution: The patch edits find_obj to skip the 'modname.name' match and to filter fuzzy matches to '.classname.' whenever classname is set. It touches the correct root-cause function, but the guard is far too broad: it now blocks ALL module-level object resolution from within a class context, not just the spurious data/attribute links.
summary.overall_assessment: Request changes: the patch fixes the reported symptom but introduces a high-severity correctness regression -- legitimate refspecific references to module-level objects from a class context (e.g. parameter/return :type: annotations in class methods referencing module-level classes, and :any: references) stop resolving.

defects.description: The added 'if not classname' guard prevents find_obj from ever matching 'modname.name' when a class context is present, and the fuzzy filter '.classname.' also excludes module-level names. Because refspecific searchmode=1 is used for field type xrefs (PyTypedField/PyXrefMixin sets refspecific=True) and for :any: references, a legitimate module-level object referenced from within a class no longer resolves. Verified: with the patch, find_obj('pkg','Foo','Config','class',1) returns [] where module-level class 'pkg.Config' exists (baseline returns [('pkg.Config',...)]). This breaks common cases such as a class method's ':type param: Config' or ':rtype: Config' referring to a module-level class.
defects.suggestion: Do not blanket-skip module-level resolution when a class is in context. Instead narrow the fix to the specific failing objtype (data/attribute nonlocal linking), e.g. only suppress the 'modname.name' fallback for the reported instance-variable case (matching upstream's targeted fix) so that class/function/module references from class context still resolve to module-level objects.

defects.description: The patch pins numerous unrelated dependency versions in setup.py and adds '-rA' to tox.ini, which are unrelated to the bug fix and constitute out-of-scope changes.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/viewcode.py, collect_pages() (connected to html-collect-pages) generated module source pages for epub builders without checking viewcode_enable_epub, unlike doctree_read() which already guards against epub.
summary.solution: The patch adds `if app.builder.name.startswith('epub') and not env.config.viewcode_enable_epub: return` at the start of collect_pages(), exactly matching the guard used in doctree_read and my proposed fix. This addresses the root cause at the point where the epub module pages are created. The patch also adds two tests verifying _modules is absent when disabled and present when enabled. Unrelated changes to setup.py (dependency pins) and tox.ini (pytest flag) are scope creep but do not affect correctness.

summary.problem: In sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py, Google-style _convert_type_spec did not tokenize type specifications (unlike the NumPy version), so union types written with '|' (e.g. 'bytes | str') were not split into individual cross-references, and the tokenizer regex (_token_regex) had no delimiter for the pipe character.
summary.solution: The patch adds '|' as a delimiter in _token_regex and rewrites Google-style _convert_type_spec to tokenize/recombine/convert type specs (mirroring the NumPy implementation), moving the shared helpers (_tokenize_type_spec, _token_type, _recombine_set_tokens) above the GoogleDocstring class. This fixes the root cause at the point where the type string is parsed/converted, and it covers both the Google and NumPy code paths so no sibling path is left unpatched.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch addresses the root cause (napoleon type-spec conversion) rather than a symptom; all 49 napoleon tests and 45 py-domain tests pass, and functional verification confirms 'bytes | str' now renders as ':class:`bytes` | :class:`str`'.

defects.description: The patch includes unrelated dependency version pins (Jinja2<3.0, markupsafe<=2.0.1, alabaster<0.7.12, sphinxcontrib-* upper bounds) and a tox.ini change (-rA), which are environment-compatibility tweaks unrelated to the union-type feature. They are functionally harmless but constitute scope creep.

summary.problem: In sphinx/util/inspect.py, object_description() had no special handling for enum.Enum values, so it fell through to repr(), rendering defaults as '<MyEnum.ValueA: 10>' instead of 'MyEnum.ValueA'.
summary.solution: The patch adds a branch in object_description() that returns str(object) when the object is an enum.Enum instance. This is exactly the root-cause location (where the description string is created) and matches my proposed fix. str() on an Enum yields 'MyEnum.ValueA', producing the expected signature. The patch also adds unit and autodoc tests, plus unrelated harmless version-pinning in setup.py/tox.ini.
summary.overall_assessment: The fix correctly addresses the root cause at the point of creation in object_description(); all 111 tests in the inspect and autodoc suites pass and behavior verification confirms the exact expected output.

summary.problem: In sphinx/cmd/quickstart.py, do_prompt was called with the is_path validator (and default='') for the 'Please enter a new root path (or just Enter to exit)' prompt; is_path rejects empty input via ValidationError, so pressing Enter looped forever and the sys.exit(1) path was never reached.
summary.solution: The patch adds a new is_path_or_empty validator that returns '' for empty input while still validating non-empty paths, and uses it at the prompt (line ~232). This fixes the root cause at the point where empty input was wrongly rejected, allowing do_prompt to return '' and trigger the existing sys.exit(1). It matches the identified root cause exactly and adds a passing regression test.

summary.problem: In sphinx/pycode/ast.py, visit_Tuple joined elements with ', ' and appended ')', so a single-element tuple (1,) rendered as (1) losing the required trailing comma.
summary.solution: The patch special-cases len(node.elts) == 1 in visit_Tuple to append ',)' instead of ')', keeping the trailing comma while leaving multi-element and empty tuples unchanged. This is exactly the root-cause location and logic. It also adds the requested test case, plus unrelated setup.py/tox.ini dependency pinning that does not affect correctness.

summary.problem: Root cause is in sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py PropertyDocumenter.can_document_member/import_object (and get_class_members in importer.py): a method decorated with @classmethod @property is stored in the class __dict__ as a classmethod wrapping a property, so inspect.isproperty(member) is False and getattr returns the computed value, meaning autodoc never recognizes/documents it as a property.
summary.solution: The patch does not touch any autodoc source at all. It only edits setup.py (pins sphinxcontrib-*, Jinja2, alabaster, markupsafe versions) and tox.ini (adds pytest -rA flag). None of these changes affect how PropertyDocumenter detects or documents classmethod+property members, so it does not match the root cause.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch is entirely unrelated to the reported bug and cannot fix it; classmethod+property methods will still go undocumented.

defects.description: The bug (undocumented @classmethod @property methods) is caused by PropertyDocumenter.can_document_member relying on inspect.isproperty(member), which is False for a classmethod-wrapped property, and by the imported object being the computed value rather than the property. The patch makes no change here whatsoever.
defects.suggestion: Update PropertyDocumenter.can_document_member and import_object to detect classmethod-wrapped properties (unwrap classmethod via __func__ to obtain the property, set self.object to that property, and mark it as a classmethod property), plus add an inspect helper.

summary.problem: In sphinx/domains/python.py, PyProperty.handle_signature added the property's :type: annotation as plain text (desc_annotation(typ, ': ' + typ)) instead of parsing it, so types were never cross-referenced.
summary.solution: The patch replaces the plain-text annotation with `_parse_annotation(typ, self.env)` and builds the annotation from those nodes, exactly mirroring PyAttribute.handle_signature. This is at the root-cause location and produces pending_xref nodes, so property types are now cross-referenced. It also updates the corresponding test and pins some dependency versions in setup.py/tox.ini (env-only, non-functional).
summary.overall_assessment: The fix targets the exact root cause and matches PyAttribute's correct behavior; all domain_py tests pass and an end-to-end check confirms a pending_xref is emitted for the property type.

summary.problem: In sphinx/domains/python.py, _parse_annotation()/unparse() renders constant values (e.g. True/False in Literal[...]) as plain nodes.Text, which the post-processing loop then converts into py:class pending_xref nodes, causing nitpick (-n -W) to fail because True is not a class.
summary.solution: The patch threads an inside_literal flag through unparse(), detects Literal subscripts (Name 'Literal' or typing/typing_extensions.Literal), and renders constant values inside Literal as desc_sig_keyword / desc_sig_literal_number / desc_sig_literal_string nodes instead of nodes.Text. Because these are not Text nodes, the xref-conversion loop skips them, so literal values no longer become py:class cross references. This matches the root cause location and depth exactly.
summary.overall_assessment: The patch fixes the root cause at the correct location; bug reproduction (Literal[True] no longer xrefs 'True') and regression (List[int] still xrefs) verified, and the full test_domain_py.py (46) and test_ext_autodoc.py (71) suites pass.

defects.description: The patch also pins numerous unrelated dependencies (sphinxcontrib-*, Jinja2<3.0, alabaster<0.7.12, markupsafe<=2.0.1) and edits tox.ini (adds -rA). These are environment/scope-creep changes unrelated to the Literal nitpick bug fix, though they do not break the fix or tests.

summary.problem: In sphinx/util/typing.py restify(), a mocked base class taken from __orig_bases__ is a _MockObject instance whose __qualname__ is '' (set in _MockObject.__init__), so restify rendered 'torch.nn.' instead of 'torch.nn.Module' in the class 'Bases' section.
summary.solution: The patch adds an early branch in restify() that detects mocked objects via __sphinx_mock__ and renders them using their __display_name__ (e.g. 'torch.nn.Module'), and generalizes ismock() to detect _MockObject anywhere in the MRO. This targets exactly the root-cause location (restify) where the wrong string was produced, not merely the crash site.
summary.overall_assessment: The fix is at the correct root-cause location, verified to output ':py:class:`torch.nn.Module`' for the reported case, and all autodoc/typing/mock tests pass with no regressions.

summary.problem: In sphinx/domains/python.py, PyMethod.get_index_text() generated the index entry for the :property: option as '%s() (%s property)' with parentheses, whereas properties should not have parens.
summary.solution: The patch changes line 799 from '%s() (%s property)' to '%s (%s property)', removing the parentheses. This is exactly the root-cause location (point of index-text creation) and makes PyMethod+:property: consistent with PyProperty.get_index_text. Sibling paths (classmethod/staticmethod/method) correctly retain parens. The corresponding test in test_domain_py.py is updated. The patch also includes unrelated setup.py dependency pins and a corrupted tox.ini py311 URL edit.
